name: testing-pipeline
statement: The internal home of Aviary: a terminal and on-chain products built on [Pipeline](https://github.com/MetalLegBob/pipeline), a permissionless router for experimental Solana markets.
destination:
A build-ready spec for the five products on devnet (Pipescope, the containment hook, the tax AMM, Pool4 for Solana and the lending pool) in `docs/spec/` (a shared `README.md` plus one file per product), with decisions in `docs/adr/`, and for each product a set of `build` tickets whose run order `## Next` gives the relay.
It is released in stages: each product's build tickets are cut as soon as its own decisions close, so building starts before the whole map is done.

rule.name: Built for MetalLegBob
rule.text: every decision the owner makes is a default he may change.

tickets.resolution:
| Working name | Public name | In prose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the suite | **Aviary** | the suite |
| Pipescope | **Aviary** (the suite and its terminal share the name) | Aviary |

| tax AMM | **Aviary Tax AMM** | the tax AMM |
| Pool4 for Solana | **Aviary Buy Wall AMM**, credited as a port of IMD's Pool4 design | the buy wall AMM |

- Address `aviary.trade` and X handle `@aviarytrade`, neither registered yet: Owner: register aviary.trade and @aviarytrade.
- The repo and folder keep the internal name `testing-pipeline`.

## What landed

Rename the suite and its products to their public names renamed `GLOSSARY.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the ADRs and every spec file, and added "Names" to [`docs/spec/README.md`](/spec/README/).

- Code identifiers carry no public name: the `pipescope-*` apps, packages, Workers and database in the architecture spec became `terminal-*`.
- Left as they were: file names (`docs/spec/pipescope*.md`, `pool4-for-solana.md`, `lending-pool.md`, the ADR files) and ticket titles, so links still work, and `research/` and `docs/charting-brief.md`, which are dated records.

## What the lookups found (2026-11-10)

Free lookups only: RDAP for domains (whois for `.so` and `.io`), and X's public embed endpoint for handles, without signing in.
"Free" means no registration record; the price shows only at a registrar's checkout and may be a premium one.
For a handle, "no live account" can also be a suspended or reserved handle.
No trademark search was done, only web searches for same-name projects.

| Name | `.trade` | `.markets` | X, bare name | X, name + `trade` | Same-name projects found |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Aviary | free | free | no live account | free | AviaryAI (banking software); no crypto project |
| Quirk | free | free | taken | free | Quirk, a UK personal finance app; Quirkies NFTs |
| Telltale | free | taken | taken | free | Telltale Games |
| Leftfield | free | free | taken | free | none |
| Offshoot | free | free | taken | free | none |

`.com` was taken for all of them, and for about seventy other candidates.
`canary.trade`, `.fun`, `.fi`, `.xyz` and `.app` were all taken, so Canary stays the checks' name and carries nothing else.

Each is the owner's default; any of them can change.

1. **Does the suite have one public name or two (suite and terminal)?**
   Answer: one; the suite and its terminal share it, since our other products live inside the terminal and have no sites of their own.
   Alternatives: a separate suite brand above the terminal; keeping Pipescope, dropped because it borrows Pipeline's name.
   Lives in: `GLOSSARY.md` (Aviary, Suite); `docs/spec/README.md`, Names.
   To change: spec only.
2. **What is the name?**
   Answer: Aviary. It is where the canary lives, with every strange bird on show, which fits "everything listed, nothing curated".
   Alternatives: Quirk (runner-up), Telltale, Leftfield, Offshoot; Canary itself, whose domains are taken.
   Lives in: `GLOSSARY.md`; `docs/spec/README.md`, Names; in code, one config module, `apps/terminal-web/src/brand.ts`.
   To change: a config value plus a sweep of the docs.
3. **How are the on-chain products named?**
   Answer: plain descriptive names with the suite's name in front in public: Aviary Tax AMM, Aviary Containment Hook, Aviary Buy Wall AMM, Aviary Lending AMM.
   Alternatives: a brand name per product; descriptive names with no prefix.
   Lives in: `docs/spec/README.md`, Names; each program's strategy metadata `name` and the `name` in its `security.txt`.
   To change: a metadata update for a strategy; a build-time constant for `security.txt`, so before deployment.
4. **Does our Pool4 port carry the name Pool4?**
   Answer: no; it is the buy wall AMM, and it credits IMD's Pool4 design wherever it is described.
   Alternatives: Pool4 for Solana (the working name), which reads as IMD's own release; burn AMM; capped burn AMM.
   Lives in: `GLOSSARY.md` (Buy wall AMM, Buy wall market); `docs/spec/pool4-for-solana.md`.
   To change: spec only, plus the metadata name.
5. **Is the lending product a "pool" or an "AMM"?**
   Answer: the lending AMM, because a lending pool reads as a pool to lend to or borrow from, and the three strategies then read as one family.
   Alternatives: lending pool (the working name).
   Lives in: `GLOSSARY.md` (Lending AMM); `docs/spec/lending-pool.md`.
   To change: spec only, plus the metadata name.
6. **Which address and handle?**
   Answer: `aviary.trade` and `@aviarytrade`, a matching pair; no defensive domains.
   Alternatives: `aviary.markets`, `aviary.exchange`, `aviary.so`, `aviary.fun` (all unregistered on 2026-11-10); bare `@aviary` if X will give it.
   Lives in: `docs/spec/README.md`, Names; `docs/spec/pipescope-architecture.md`, Environments; the same config module as the name.
   To change: a config value and a domain; nothing is registered yet.
7. **Do code identifiers carry the public name?**
   Answer: no; apps, packages, Workers, databases, crates and programs are named for what they are (`terminal-web`, `tax-amm`), so a rename never touches them.
   Alternatives: `aviary-*` identifiers; keeping `pipescope-*`.
   Lives in: `docs/spec/README.md`, Names; `docs/spec/pipescope-architecture.md`, Repo layout.
   To change: spec only until the first build ticket creates them.
8. **Do spec files and tickets take the new names?**
   Answer: not now; they keep the names they were written under so existing links work, and Cut Pipescope's build tickets may name its merged file `aviary.md`.
   Alternatives: renaming the files and fixing every link in the map and the closed tickets.
   Lives in: `docs/spec/README.md`, Product files.
   To change: spec only.

tickets.title: Pool4 for Solana design
tickets.resolution:
- **Fee**: chosen per market at creation, 0.25% to 3%, never changeable, and always taken in SOL (from the SOL paid in on a buy, from the SOL paid out on a sell), on top of Pipeline's 0.25%.
- **Trim split**: a reward share of 0% to 30% per market goes to one rewards recipient and the rest is burned; all trimmed SOL becomes the buy wall, and tokens the wall buys go through the same split.
- **Staking**: not in v1; a rewards recipient can be a staking program later.
- **Keeper jobs**: four permissionless custom actions, `place_wall`, `settle`, `pay_rewards` and `sweep_fees`. Only `place_wall` tips: the lower of 0.002 SOL and the market's fee rate times the SOL handled, once 0.01 SOL is idle or spent.
- **Containment hook**: optional by design, but not in v1, because [Containment hook policy](/18/) closed during this session with a first version that binds only tax AMM markets. Pool4 for Solana works with plain mints and keeps what a later hook version would need (router-only counters, SOL-only fees and tips, liquidity that can never leave).
- **Parameters**: per market, fixed at creation: the fee, the wall split, the reward share, both recipients, the cap floor (0.1% to 100% of the seeded tokens) and the cap decay (0% to 100% a day). Fixed for every market: the cap starts at the seeded tokens, a buy lowers it by all the room it opens, the buy wall's crawl of about 4% a day behind a lagged reference, and the keeper thresholds. Pipescope's form pre-fills IMD's own launch values.
- **Where it leaves IMD's design**: rates per second, not per block; at most one day of cap decay allowance builds up while idle; no owner powers at all (IMD's owner can close the market and withdraw everything).
- **Markets**: anyone creates one, seeded by a launchpad in one call or created and seeded in one transaction; liquidity is locked for good; nobody controls a market afterwards, except that each recipient may hand its own role to another wallet. The token trades against wrapped SOL, with its mint and freeze authorities removed and only the tax AMM's extension allowlist; exact-in only; bypass refused.
- **Upgrades can never strand a market**: a fixed-size market state with a layout version and reserved space, a release gate that replays every live market against a new build before it deploys, and fixtures of every released layout in CI. Frozen before mainnet.
- **Checked before writing**: the pricing, trim, ratchet, wall and keeper rules ran as an integer model for 3,000 random sequences (about 957,000 swaps) with every invariant holding; the spec's worked example is the model's output, for the build to reproduce exactly.

One correction to what I told the owner while grilling: I said the reward share would wait in the vault until a contained token's unlock.
The hook's spec allows payouts out of a home vault, and its first version does not bind Pool4 for Solana markets at all, so the spec has no such wait; `pay_rewards` stays a separate action so burns never depend on a transfer.

For other tickets:

- Cut Pool4 for Solana's build tickets is unblocked by this ticket; a suggested slicing is posted there.
- The keeper runner (the map's "Not yet specified") has Pool4 for Solana's part: the four jobs and when to run each, in the spec's "For the keeper runner".
- `docs/spec/README.md` lists its product files but not yet this one, the containment hook's or the lending pool's.

| ID (proposed) | Question | Answer (the owner's default) | Alternatives weighed | Where it lives, and how it changes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POOL4-02 | What fee does a market charge? | Chosen per market at creation, 0.25% to 3%, never changeable; the create form pre-fills 1%. | IMD's fixed 1%; 0.5% swept plus 0.15% kept by the pool. | "Constants" (`MIN_FEE_BPS`, `MAX_FEE_BPS`) and "Creation parameters". Bounds are build-time constants, the rate a creation parameter, the pre-fill a form default. |
| POOL4-03 | In which token is the fee taken? | Always SOL: from the SOL paid in on a buy and the SOL paid out on a sell. | On whichever token comes in, as IMD does. | "Pricing" and "The fee". Code, before deployment. |
| POOL4-06 | What happens to trimmed tokens and SOL? | A reward share of 0% to 30% per market (the form pre-fills 15%) goes to one rewards recipient and the rest is burned; all trimmed SOL becomes the buy wall; tokens the wall buys go through the same split. | Burning everything; IMD's fixed 85/15 with its three-way reward split. | "Constants" (`MAX_REWARD_SHARE_BPS`), "Creation parameters" and "Keeper jobs". The limit is a build-time constant; the share and recipient are creation parameters. |
| POOL4-07 | Is staking with streamed rewards in v1? | No; a rewards recipient can be a staking program later. | Shipping a staking vault and dripper with v1, as IMD has. | "Not in v1". Spec only. |
| POOL4-08 | Does it pair with the containment hook? | Not in v1: the hook's first version binds only tax AMM markets. Pool4 for Solana works with plain mints and keeps everything a later hook version would need. | Requiring the hook; making these markets home markets in v1. | "With the containment hook". The hook's program and spec. |
| POOL4-09 | How are markets created? | By anyone: seeded by a launchpad in one call, or created and seeded by the creator in one transaction. One seed, locked for good. | Only by graduation from one bonding curve. | "Markets". Code. |
| POOL4-10 | Who controls a market after the seed? | Nobody, us included: no close, no withdrawal, no parameter change. Each of the two recipients may hand its own role to another wallet. | IMD's owner powers (close, withdraw, change every parameter); recipients fixed for good. | "What it is" and "Recipients". Code. |
| POOL4-11 | Which parameters does a creator choose? | Per market: the fee, the wall split, the reward share, both recipients, the cap floor (0.1% to 100% of the seeded tokens) and the cap decay (0% to 100% of them a day). Fixed for all: the cap starts at the seeded tokens, a buy lowers it by all the room it opens, the wall's guard rates and the keeper thresholds. The form pre-fills a floor of 20% and a decay of 20% a day, IMD's own ratios. | Everything per market; everything fixed. | "Constants" and "Creation parameters". Constants, creation parameters and form defaults. |
| POOL4-12 | How is the buy wall kept from being placed at a pumped price? | IMD's guard: the wall's floor drops at once with the price and rises about 4% a day toward a reference that follows the price by at most 2% per 12 seconds. | Refusing to place the wall when the price is far above a reference. | "After pricing" (`FLOOR_CRAWL_BPS`, `REF_STEP_BPS`, `REF_STEP_WINDOW`). The rates are build-time constants; the rule is code. |
| POOL4-13 | Does cap decay allowance build up while a market is idle? | For at most one day. | Without limit, as in IMD's hook. | "After pricing" (`DECAY_CREDIT_WINDOW`). Build-time constant. |
| POOL4-14 | A minimum trim size, and exact-out swaps? | No minimum trim; exact-in only in v1. | A minimum trim; exact-out across the wall. | "After pricing" and "Not in v1". Code. |
| POOL4-15 | Which keeper jobs, and what do they pay? | Four permissionless actions: place the wall, settle, pay rewards, sweep fees. Only placing the wall tips its caller: the lower of 0.002 SOL and the market's fee rate times the SOL handled, once 0.01 SOL is idle or spent. | A flat share of the work on every job; jobs only our keeper may call. | "Keeper jobs" (`WALL_THRESHOLD`, `KEEPER_TIP_CAP`). Build-time constants. |
| POOL4-16 | How do upgrades avoid stranding markets? | A fixed-size market state with a layout version and reserved space, a release gate that replays every live market against the new build, and fixtures of every released layout in CI. | Migrating accounts at each upgrade; resizable accounts. | "Market state". Code and release process. |
| POOL4-17 | Which tokens may a market hold? | The token against wrapped SOL only; the token's mint and freeze authorities removed by the seed; Token-2022 extensions on the tax AMM's allowlist. | Allowing mint and freeze authorities, as the tax AMM does; other quote mints. | "Mint rules". Code. |
| POOL4-18 | What is the mainnet upgrade policy? | Frozen before any mainnet deployment, after the designer share's wallet is set. | The shared default: a multisig with a timelock first. | "Upgrades and freezing". Spec; carried out by the mainnet launch effort. |

tickets.title: Lending pool design
tickets.decision: two-mint constant-product markets with open LP shares that lend their WSOL or USDC side to fixed Kamino reserves through cTokens; a 20% buffer rebalanced only outside 10% to 30% by a permissionless keeper job; a swap redeems its shortfall in the swap and never deposits; withdraw mode when Kamino's free liquidity falls below 5 times our position; all yield and the LP fee to LPs, who bear Kamino's losses and can always leave in kind; no admin, frozen before mainnet; Kamino only ([spec](/spec/lending-pool/), Kamino facts)
tickets.resolution:
Decided with the owner in three rounds; the spec is [`docs/spec/lending-pool.md`](/spec/lending-pool/) (merged in #38), and the Kamino facts checked for it are lending-market-kamino-facts.md on the research branch.

**The ticket's questions**

- **Buffer and rebalance:** a fixed 20% of the lent side's total, rebalanced back to 20% only when it leaves the 10% to 30% band, with a dust floor; the same for every market.
- **Keeper job:** `rebalance` is a permissionless custom action that does nothing inside the band; our keeper runner calls it when Pipescope's indexer sees a market leave its band, plus a sweep every 10 minutes; no tip. One keeper job per market; no withdrawal-ticket job.
- **Mints:** exactly one lent side per market, WSOL or USDC, each tied to one Kamino reserve compiled into the program per cluster (mainnet: the main market's SOL and USDC reserves; devnet: our own Kamino lending market); creators never pick a reserve. The other side follows the tax AMM's mint rules, so hooked tokens are allowed (the hooked transfer and the Kamino redeem are sibling calls and never stack) and transfer-fee or permanent-delegate mints are refused.
- **Swaps larger than the buffer:** a swap redeems just the shortfall from Kamino in the same swap, and never deposits; the quote reads Kamino's free liquidity, withdrawal cap and flags, so a trade above buffer plus what Kamino can pay is refused cleanly.
- **Yield:** all to LPs through share value, with the LP fee (creator-set, 0% to 2%, default 0.30%); no cut for us or the creator.

**The research comment's nine questions**

1. Swaps redeem the shortfall in the swap (above).
2. Only WSOL and USDC are lent.
3. Mainnet: main market SOL `d4A2...` and USDC `D6q6...`; devnet: our own lending market, whose reserves need only a non-default price key (we name the live devnet Pyth feeds so a test borrower can create utilisation).
4. cTokens are valued everywhere at the reserve's stored rate (lag 2 to 68 s, about 0.05 bps an hour), from the reserve's own fields; LPs bear Kamino's written-off losses pro rata.
5. Near full utilisation: withdraw mode, entered when Kamino's free liquidity is below 5 times our lent value and left above 10 times; withdrawal tickets are off on the main market.
6. Kamino's switches: no admin of our own; blocked cToken deposits skip deposits, emergency mode or a deprecated reserve leaves swaps on the buffer alone, and LPs can always leave in kind (other side, buffer share, cTokens) without calling Kamino.
7. Farm rewards attach only to obligations and pay nothing on SOL and USDC today, so cToken holders miss nothing.
8. Kamino only, isolated in one module; Jupiter Lend is out of scope for this map.
9. LiteSVM tests on klend's deployed program with cloned reserves (in-swap redeem at one extra outer level with a hooked token, every Kamino state by edited account data, Kamino's real `socialize_loss`), plus a devnet demo on our own lending market including withdraw mode and emergency mode.

**Also decided:** constant-product pricing over total reserves; open LP shares with a locked minimum and `lock_lp` for protocol-owned liquidity; adds go to the buffer; removals are pro rata, in cash or in kind; bypass refused; exact-in only; market address `["market", other_mint, lent_mint, lp_fee_bps]`; seeding supported at a seeder-scoped address; frozen before mainnet, refusing to price if Kamino's reserve layout changes.

Cut the lending pool's build tickets now has its product file; it still needs `docs/spec/README.md` from [Engineering and security bar for our on-chain programs](/4/).

Follow-up merged in #42: the spec now also carries what `docs/spec/README.md` asks of each product (compute ceilings, layer-3 invariants, no accepted `pipeline-check` warnings, and the mainnet upgrade policy: frozen before mainnet, a stated departure from the shared multisig-then-freeze default). Cut the lending pool's build tickets has both files it needs.

tickets.title: Containment hook policy
tickets.decision: a contained token moves only into or out of its one tax AMM home market (no wallet-to-wallet transfers, no integrator fee accounts); a write-once `bind` signed by the mint authority fixes the market, a goal and a deadline of at most 90 days; anyone may unlock once the market's tax collected (in the quote mint, not volume) reaches the goal or the deadline passes, from a Pipescope button, no keeper; frozen before mainnet ([spec](/spec/containment-hook/), ADR 0006)
tickets.resolution:
- **Transfers while contained**: only into or out of the home market's vault or its Pipeline fee account. Every wallet-to-wallet transfer is refused, including between your own wallets and to a CEX deposit address. A buy may deliver the token to anyone, who can then only sell it back.
- **Integrator fees**: no integrator fee accounts are allowed, so sells of a contained token carry no integrator fee. This is already Pipescope's rule, since it charges only on SOL or USDC input.
- **Home market**: exactly one per token. In v1 it is a tax AMM market with its tax side on the quote mint.
- **Unlock goal**: the home market's `tax_collected`, in the quote mint, not volume. A tax authority can lower the tax to 0 within its fixed range and the tax AMM has no LP fee, so faked volume would cost only Pipeline's 0.25%. Counting tax means forcing an early unlock always costs a third party the whole goal. There is no minimum age.
- **Who sets it**: the launcher, at binding. `bind` is signed by the mint authority and write-once, and nothing can change the config afterwards, us included. It goes after `create_market` and `init_fee_account` and before the tax AMM's seed. The hook refuses every transfer until `bind`. Launchpad graduation through `pipeline_seed_liquidity` is not in v1.
- **Mint rules at binding**: an extension allowlist matching the tax AMM's (transfer hook, metadata, group); everything else is refused. The freeze authority must be unset.
- **Fallback**: a required unlock deadline, at most 90 days after binding. After it, the unlock is due even if the goal was never met.
- **Who triggers the unlock**: anyone. `unlock` is permissionless and clears both the hook program and its authority. Pipescope shows an Unlock button. There is no keeper job in v1.
- **Launch**: a devnet CLI script. Pipescope v1 doesn't launch tokens, and its tax AMM launch form refuses mints hooked by us.
- **Engineering**: start from `test-hook`'s code but replace its fail-open path with the fail-closed allow rule. The hook is frozen before any mainnet use. Ceilings are `Execute` 10k, `bind` 60k and `unlock` 30k CU. Five invariants for the fuzzing layer.

Answers to the questions posted here from [Tax AMM rules](/19/):
1. The unlock reads `tax_collected`, with the tax side on the quote mint and no minimum age.
2. Wash trading is answered by counting tax collected, so no minimum tax range is needed.
3. The hosted API's refusal of hooked input mints is in the spec: Pipescope builds those swaps with the SDK.

tickets.title: Pipescope architecture
tickets.decision: everything on the existing Cloudflare account, where Workers Paid was already active (nothing bought): an API Worker holding the indexer, live rooms and Canary's Container, and a Next.js web Worker; Postgres on a new Neon project as the only record; our own indexer, with Pipeline's hosted API only a test oracle, holding its socket only while someone watches so the account stays inside its allowance; the API prepares and simulates every transaction; Canary natively in a Container with no network, fed one snapshot a market by a Durable Object per strategy version; verified builds on GitHub Actions; explanations generated on the owner's Mac after approval, no LLM key in Cloudflare; a public rate-limited API; owner tasks: Pipescope's own Helius key, the Neon project, a GitHub token ([spec](/spec/pipescope-architecture/), ADR 0003, ADR 0004, ADR 0005)
tickets.resolution:
Resolved with the owner on 2026-11-10 (all recommendations accepted). Spec: [`docs/spec/pipescope-architecture.md`](/spec/pipescope-architecture/), merged in #35.

- **Platform**: everything on the owner's existing Cloudflare account, as two Workers, `pipescope-api` (Hono API, indexer and live-room Durable Objects, the Canary Container, crons) and `pipescope-web` (Next.js 16 through OpenNext).
  **No purchase**: Workers Paid is already active (Top-pad's vision Container runs on the account; Containers need Workers Paid).
- **Data**: Postgres on a new Neon free project through Hyperdrive with its cache off, the only system of record (ADR 0004).
- **Indexer**: our own, ported from Top-pad, on the router and every strategy program, with reconciliation, registry snapshots, a ProgramData watch and a full backfill; Pipeline's hosted devnet API is only a test oracle (ADR 0003).
  It holds its socket only while someone watches a page, because a second always-awake indexer would push the account (shared with Top-pad, whose indexer uses about 310,000 of the 400,000 GB-s a month) past its Durable Object allowance; otherwise a cron each minute.
  Market accounts are re-read after each event; no account subscriptions; no webhook spike.
- **RPC**: Pipescope's own free Helius key (owner task).
- **Trading path**: the API prepares and simulates every transaction (swap, custom action, create market) and returns it with the outcome and balance changes; the wallet signs and sends; the page reports the signature (Top-pad's fast path). Quotes are RPC simulations of `pipeline_quote`; the Container is never on the trading path. Fee rate, fee mints and fee accounts are Worker vars.
- **Canary runner**: native Rust `crates/canary` in a Cloudflare Container (`basic`, internet off), one Durable Object per strategy version, router loaded from its deployed bytes, a seam to switch from `simulate_swap` to direct calls plus settlement (ADR 0005).
- **Verified builds**: a GitHub Actions workflow started by the API, with an untrusted build job and a trusted compare job; a match is evidence, never proof.
- **Metadata fetcher**: in the API, on events and hourly, with size, type, timeout and redirect limits.
- **Explainer**: the API builds and stores the evidence per key; `pnpm explainer:approve` on the owner's Mac calls the model and writes the ledger; no LLM key in Cloudflare.
- **API**: public read and prepare endpoints, rate-limited per IP, unstable until v1.
- **Copied from Top-pad** (`b833a7b`): the indexer core, the Indexer Durable Object, candles, live rooms, Drizzle and migrations, the API and web scaffolds, the Container pattern, Playwright and the restart test; not the Codama clients.
- Glossary: Verified build, Canary run.

Owner tasks before the build: Pipescope's own Helius key, the Neon project `pipescope-devnet`, and a fine-grained GitHub token for the verify workflow.

Follow-up #40 fitted the Canary runner section to [`pipescope-canary.md`](/spec/pipescope-canary/), merged meanwhile: a `CanaryRun` runs a strategy version on all its markets or one, posts one snapshot a market and fetches accounts the binary names as missing; the spec's triggers (new markets, a sweep every 6 hours) and its RPC and Container budget are in.

tickets.title: Canary checks on the four devnet strategies
tickets.decision: Canary runs Pipeline's `pipeline-check` unchanged and adds trader-side checks (readability, the exit test over sizes, waits, the launch clock, wallets, transferred tokens and a queue of buyers, quote against swap, cost, direct calls, token authorities acting); only what an ordinary 0.01 SOL trade meets now can fail (95% back passes, under 50% fails) and conditional findings warn; custom instructions are listed, not called; it runs on upgrades, on market creation and every 6 hours ([spec](/spec/pipescope-canary/), harness and results)
tickets.resolution:
The decisions are in [`docs/spec/pipescope-canary.md`](/spec/pipescope-canary/), not in `pipescope.md` as this ticket's body says: `pipescope.md` belongs to Pipescope v1 scope, and the map gives each Pipescope ticket its own file.
The harness and its output are on the throwaway branch `prototype/canary-checks` (an orphan branch, never merged): `src/main.rs`, one JSON file per market and `summary.md`.

### What was run

A LiteSVM harness on Pipeline's Apache-2.0 crates at `5ad130d` (cloned into a scratchpad for reading, pulled through Cargo for building, never copied here), on all 61 devnet markets of 8 strategies, at slots 520,628,944 to 520,629,552.
It clones each market with `pipeline-check`'s own cloner, runs `pipeline-check` on the snapshot, then trades the same snapshot through the real router with signature checks off: 2,718 swaps in about two and a half minutes and 442 RPC requests.

### What Canary found beyond `pipeline-check` and the trust flags

- `EZwLuZ...` (a sniper tax) passes `pipeline-check` 14 of 14; with the clock set back to a market's creation a 0.01 SOL round trip returns 0.995%, then 11.9% after 10 seconds, 66.7% after 1 minute and 99.5% from 10 minutes on.
- The outside builder's AMM returns 48.8% to 49.4% on an immediate round trip on all 4 markets; `pipeline-check`'s `round_trip` passes, because it warns only about a profit.
- On the 3 open bonding curves a buy of 1 SOL or more completes the curve and cannot be sold back there; buys of 0.1 SOL and less return 97.5% to 98.6%. (`pipeline-check` warns on these too; Canary adds the size boundary.)
- 16 of 61 markets cannot be read by their own strategy's current version: 6 of 8 on the Pool4 port, 6 of 7 on `2Tmcmq...`, 2 of 3 on `4scUVy...`, 2 of 23 on the constant product. `pipeline-check` fails each one as an account-resolution failure; Canary names it and counts it per strategy version.
- Acting as a token's authority: minting and selling takes 99.0% of the SOL in a constant-product market's vault; with the Token-2022 transfer fee set to 100%, a 0.01 SOL buy takes the SOL and delivers nothing. The flags only say the authority exists.
- 34 instructions beyond Pipeline's own across the 8 strategies, each confirmed by its discriminator in the code.
- Clean everywhere: all 2,658 swaps that had a quote matched it to the unit; insiders' wallets, transferred tokens, a queue of five buyers and waits of up to 30 days made no difference; every direct `pipeline_swap` call was refused.

### Decided with the owner

1. **Thresholds**: a round trip that returns 95% or more is a pass, 50% up to 95% a warn, under 50% (or tokens that cannot be sold) a fail; the number always shows beside the word.
2. **Conditional findings are warns**: fail is kept for what an ordinary 0.01 SOL trade meets right now; anything that depends on another time, a larger size or an authority acting is at most a warn.
3. **Custom instructions are listed, not called**: per strategy version, with who has called each and how often; Canary acts only on the standard token powers (mint, freeze, transfer fee, permanent delegate, pause).
4. **Re-runs**: at once on a strategy or router upgrade and on market creation (then 10 minutes, 1 hour and 1 day later), and every market every 6 hours.

### Taken as defaults, stated to the owner

- Canary runs `pipeline-check` unchanged and keeps its report as one result (the question the explainer spec left open).
- Canary covers every registered strategy and market, not the original four.
- Sizes are set on the money side only (0.00001 to 10 SOL, reference 0.01 SOL), and a sale only sells what a buy in the same run produced; sizing by the token vault sold tokens that could not exist and gave false alarms.
- "A buyer could not sell back", for the trade-box notice that Pipescope v1 scope asked about, is any exit-test result where a buy worked and the sale of what it bought failed, fail or warn, with its condition stated.

### The 6002 from the quoter-hosting input

Confirmed as suspected: it is the constant-product strategy's own `WrongAccount` (6002), raised at `test-strategy-cp/src/lib.rs:199` because the sale was given the buy direction's vault, not the router's `ListingFeeTooHigh`.
`Quoter::simulate_swap` prints only the last log line, where the router repeats the code.
With the sale's own vault the same sale succeeds, so that failure is no evidence that devnet's router differs from its source (`probe6002.txt`).

### Left for later

Canary calling custom instructions (a fee change through `UpdateConfig`, say) needs each strategy's argument layout; it goes to the map's "Not yet specified".

tickets.title: Engineering and security bar for our on-chain programs
tickets.decision: Anchor 1.2.2 on Pipeline's pins, strategies from its template; bypass refused; LiteSVM through the real devnet router, Proptest and Kani on the maths, stateful invariant fuzzing, `pipeline-check` with no Fail or Warn, a devnet demo; a last hardening ticket per program with Stronghold of Security and Book of Knowledge; solana-verify builds, source public under Apache-2.0, complete metadata; upgradeable on devnet under one key, shown like anyone's ([spec](/spec/README/))
tickets.resolution:
The full bar is in [`docs/spec/README.md`](/spec/README/) (PR #34), read against Pipeline `5ad130d`.
In short, every on-chain program, before its build tickets count as done on devnet:

- **Framework:** Anchor `=1.2.2` with Pipeline's pins (Rust 1.97.1, cargo-build-sbf 4.6.0, sBPF v3, LiteSVM 0.18.2, Kani 0.67.0), moving when Pipeline moves; native or Pinocchio only on a measured compute need.
- **Starting point:** strategies from Pipeline's Apache-2.0 strategy template, the containment hook from its `test-hook`; Pipeline crates pinned by `rev`.
- **Strategy rules:** refuse bypass (ADR 0001); quote and swap share one pricing function.
- **Test layers:** LiteSVM through the real devnet router (fetched and pinned by hash) with hostile cases; Proptest and Kani (Z3 for rounding) on pure maths; stateful Proptest invariant fuzzing instead of Trident (stuck on solana-sdk 2.3); `pipeline-check` with zero Fail and zero Warn in tests and against devnet; compute ceilings and call depth; cloned mainnet state for outside protocols; a scripted devnet demo; Canary checks once they exist. One CI workflow gates merges.
- **Internal adversarial review:** a hardening ticket per program, last, in a fresh session: Stronghold of Security plus Book of Knowledge (MetalLegBob's Solana Vibes Kit), fixes with `sos_<id>` regression tests, then a verify round; no open Critical, High or Medium; Lows only with the owner's sign-off. `/code-review` on every build PR.
- **Verified builds:** solana-verify Docker builds with Pipeline's pins, hashes compared on devnet, deploys recorded in `deployments/devnet.json`, `security.txt` embedded.
- **Published source:** from this repo, public before the first on-chain devnet deploy, on-chain workspace under Apache-2.0 (ADR 0002).
- **Metadata:** complete `pipeline-strategy-metadata/1` with source, IDL and the `pipeline-check` report, committed and linked at the commit hash; `security.audits` stays empty.
- **Upgrade authority:** upgradeable on devnet under one project key, nothing frozen; Pipescope shows our programs exactly like anyone's; each product's spec states its mainnet intent (multisig and timelock, then frozen).

External audits stay with the mainnet launch effort.
The repo was still private on GitHub on 2026-11-10; the owner makes it public before the first on-chain devnet deploy.

tickets.title: Pipescope v1 scope
tickets.decision: six pages (feed, market, strategy, wallet, create market, search); everything listed, nothing curated, filters off by default; one market, one hop, exact-in, every transaction simulated before signing; a 0.5% integrator fee only when paying in SOL or USDC, into a fee wallet separate from the suite treasury, always shown in the trade box; Canary results as neutral facts, a failed exit test repeated in the trade box; every metadata form rendered as untrusted; our products live inside Pipescope ([spec](/spec/pipescope/))
tickets.resolution:
Decided with the owner over three grilling rounds; the full decisions are in [`docs/spec/pipescope.md`](/spec/pipescope/) (merged in Specify Pipescope's first devnet version), read against Pipeline at `5ad130d`.

- **Pages**: feed, market page, strategy page, wallet page, create market (from a strategy's `init` form, existing mints only) and search, plus static Fees and Devnet help pages. Out of the first version: token pages, watchlists, alerts, leaderboards, token launches, strategy registration, routing, multi-hop, exact-out, USD prices, a faucet and a native app.
- **Listing**: every strategy and market is listed and nothing is curated; filters for liquidity, volume, age and Pipeline's trust flags, all off by default; broken metadata is listed as "Metadata unavailable" with no forms.
- **Trading**: one market, one hop, exact-in, 1% default slippage; every transaction is simulated before signing, and a failed simulation keeps the sign button off.
- **Wallets**: any Solana Wallet Standard wallet through `@solana/kit`; desktop first, working at phone width, in wallets' in-app browsers and through Mobile Wallet Adapter; no native app.
- **Integrator fee**: 0.5%, charged only when the trader pays in a fee mint (SOL or USDC), into a dedicated fee wallet separate from the tax AMM's `SUITE_TREASURY`; the trade box always shows the fee breakdown, and the swap is built from the rate on screen.
- **Canary results**: neutral facts in numbers, with version and date; no scores, badges or colours; failures first, plainly worded; a failed exit test is repeated in the trade box with a one-tick acknowledgement and never blocks the trade; after an upgrade, pages show "tests and explanation for this version are pending".
- **Explainer**: one explanation per key as in `pipescope-explainer.md`, approved by the owner with one command; no admin page and none on demand; shown on strategy pages and beside each market's own facts panel.
- **Custom-action forms**: every `actions` and `init` form from any strategy's metadata, treated as untrusted (plain text, full link domains, program, instruction and accounts shown, simulation of balance changes, refused when metadata is invalid).
- **Tokens and prices**: on-chain token names always shown with the short mint address; only SOL and USDC named by us; prices in the market's own mints.
- **Shared**, for `docs/spec/README.md` later: our products get no websites of their own; each adds its panel and forms to Pipescope.

New ticket: Telegram bot for Pipescope, blocked by [Pipescope architecture](/13/), graduated from the map's fog.
Glossary: added Fee mint and Fee wallet.

tickets.title: Tax AMM rules
tickets.decision: two-mint constant-product markets with a fixed tax side and the tax outside the curve; liquidity seeded once and locked; buy and sell taxes capped at 10%, changeable only by an optional tax authority inside fixed ranges; a 10% suite share, then up to four recipients and a burn, paid by a permissionless `distribute`; no exact-out, no bypass; counters for the containment hook; a mint extension allowlist; built first, from Pipeline's strategy template ([spec](/spec/tax-amm/))
tickets.resolution:
- **Tax side**: two-mint markets; the creator picks the tax side, fixed for the market's life (Pipescope defaults it to the quote mint).
- **Pricing**: constant product with the tax outside the curve, so the curve's price stays fair; quotes include the tax.
- **Liquidity**: seeded once (a creator-signed action in the `create_market` transaction, or `pipeline_seed_liquidity`), locked for good, no LP shares or LP fee; an optional virtual reserve allows single-sided launches.
- **Rates**: a buy tax and a sell tax, each capped at 10% by the program; an optional tax authority may change them inside per-side ranges fixed at creation and change the recipients, effective immediately, and may renounce; nobody else, us included, can change anything.
- **Where it goes**: a 10% suite share first, then up to four recipients plus an optional burn (not for SOL); tax builds up in the market's vault and a permissionless `distribute` pays each slot, never during a swap.
- **Exact-out**: not in v1 (`supports_exact_out = false`).
- **Pairing with the containment hook**: bypass refused; the market state keeps volume per mint, tax collected and swap count from router swaps only, plus creation time and the fixed tax ranges, at fixed offsets; vaults are computable before creation; the program is frozen before mainnet. Which total the unlock reads and how it resists wash trading are questions posted on [Containment hook policy](/18/).
- **Mints**: Token-2022 extensions on an allowlist (transfer hook, metadata, group); everything else refused, so a tax market's mints only ever show the `token-2022`, `mint-authority`, `freeze-authority`, `transfer-hook` and `transfer-hook-authority` trust flags.
- **Building**: start from Pipeline's Apache-2.0 strategy template (`CLAUDE.md` now allows it), pinned to `5ad130d`.

tickets.title: Explainer samples for the four devnet strategies
tickets.decision: presentation A (a short summary first, full points one click away), the neutral tone and length of the samples, Claude Haiku 5.5 behind an owner approval queue (under $0.01 an explanation), prompt `explainer-v0` with an eight-check validator in code ([spec](/spec/pipescope-explainer/), samples)
tickets.resolution:
The owner judged hand-written samples for the four devnet strategies and a hostile-metadata fixture (2026-11-10).
The samples were written in the session from the evidence and prompt production would use, with no model call.

Decisions:
- **Presentation A, short first**: a summary of at most 70 words, the open questions always visible, and the full list of points one click away.
- **Tone and length right as written**: neutral, short sentences that state what the code and accounts allow, never intent; amounts as facts and purposes as "appears to"; unknowns listed, never guessed.
- **Model: Claude Haiku 5.5** (`claude-haiku-5-5`) with structured outputs; under $0.01 per explanation at today's sizes (about 2,700 tokens in and 1,000 out). The first owner-approved paid run measures how often its drafts pass the validator, and if any input fails twice the owner decides whether to move to a larger model.
- **Paid calls go through an approval queue**: new explanations wait until the owner approves them in one go, and that approval writes the spend-ledger line.

Spec: [`docs/spec/pipescope-explainer.md`](/spec/pipescope-explainer/), landed by Specify Pipescope's explainer from the owner's verdict on the samples. It holds the prompt `explainer-v0`, the output schema, the validator's eight checks, the presentation, the approval queue and the test plan.

Samples (primary source, never merged): branch `prototype/explainer-samples`. `index.html` is the samples page, `check.mjs` runs the validator, and `devnet-facts-2026-11-09.md` holds every chain fact behind the samples, read on devnet on 2026-11-09 with free-tier RPC.

What the samples showed:
- None of the four devnet strategies has metadata, an IDL or a verified build, so today's explanations rest on chain facts, observed transactions and read-only probes; only the constant product's source is public, and even that is unused until its build is verified.
- Since the 2026-11-08 21:10 UTC upgrades, 6 of the Pool4 port's 8 markets and 2 of the constant product's 20 fail every quote and swap (`AccountDidNotDeserialize`); nothing the router emits says so.
- The outside builder's market returned 48.99% of the input on a tiny round trip and trades around the router through its own buy and sell.
- The validator caught a wrong address in a hand-written sample, and it refuses the draft of a model that obeyed the hostile metadata on 13 checks.

Addendum: Build the explainer's facts on Pipeline's trust facts and metadata standard adds that Pipescope computes program and mint facts with Pipeline's own trust flags (`pipeline-client`, added 2026-11-09 after the samples), validates metadata with Pipeline's v1 parser, uses the metadata's `source` only as a lead for `solana-verify`, and keeps `security.audits` and `conformance` links as untrusted author text.

tickets.title: Run Pipeline on this Mac and on devnet
tickets.decision: Pipeline at `a2d5bfb` and `5ad130d` builds and passes all its tests here with Rust 1.97.1, cargo-build-sbf 4.6.0, platform tools v1.57 (Intel Mac), Agave 4.4.1 and Node 24, installed beside the machine's Solana 2.2.20 by `scripts/install-toolchain.sh` ([steps](/toolchain/)); the devnet wallet holds 12.9 SOL, the smoke swap passes on devnet and a local validator, warm quotes take 100 to 220 µs; Pipeline has since added a hosted devnet API, a conformance checker and trust facts
tickets.resolution:
Pipeline builds, tests and runs on the owner's Mac (iMac Pro, Intel Xeon W-2150B, x86_64, macOS 15.7.3), on a local validator and on devnet, with its toolchain installed side by side.
The machine's own Solana CLI 2.2.20 and its cargo-build-sbf are unchanged.
The steps that work, and everything below in more detail, are in [`docs/toolchain.md`](/toolchain/) (landed by PR #26).

### Toolchain and how it was installed

| Tool | Version | Installed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rust (host) | 1.97.1 | rustup toolchain, from Pipeline's `rust-toolchain.toml` |
| cargo-build-sbf | 4.6.0 | `cargo install --root ~/.local/share/testing-pipeline/toolchain/cargo-build-sbf-4.6.0`, never `~/.cargo/bin` (cargo searches that before `PATH`) |
| Platform tools | v1.57 (rustc 1.95.0, clang 22.1.2) | v1.58, the default and Pipeline's pin, has no Intel macOS build; v1.57 builds the same sBPF v3 |
| Agave CLI | 4.4.1 | release tarball checked against GitHub's SHA-256 into `~/.local/share/testing-pipeline/toolchain/agave-v4.4.1`, never through agave-install (which would switch every project's `solana`) |
| Node | 24.4.1 (nvm) | Node 26, the machine's default, breaks WebSocket confirmations on public devnet |

- `scripts/install-toolchain.sh` installs all of it, idempotently.
- `source scripts/toolchain-env.sh` puts it first on `PATH` for one shell.
- On Intel Macs the env file also puts a `cargo-build-sbf` wrapper first, which adds `--tools-version v1.57`, because Pipeline's own scripts and strategy template call a bare `cargo build-sbf`.
- On its first run cargo-build-sbf 4.6.0 removed rustup's `solana` toolchain link, which the machine's 2.2.20 uses. It was relinked, and the install script now restores it. Building with 2.2.20, then 4.6.0, showed that the two leave each other alone after that.

### Wallet

`9rYtQM57An5FRiVMkE5aZVRMtq5i1uwN3iiAEjRoywCt`, at `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/wallet.json` (mode 600).
It holds **12.936 devnet SOL**.
Funding came from the CLI: two Alchemy airdrops on 2026-11-09, then eleven 1 SOL airdrops through `devnet-airdrop` (Alchemy) between 01:25 and 02:18 UTC on 2026-11-10.
The public faucet (now HTTP 410), Helius's faucet (rate limits, then HTTP 500) and devnet-pow gave nothing.

### Tests

| Step | `a2d5bfb` | `5ad130d` (Pipeline's newest) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build the programs | 5 programs, sBPF v3, 37 s | 5 programs, one at a time as `solana-verify` builds them, 52 s |
| LiteSVM `cargo test --workspace` | 425 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored (82 binaries) | 464 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored doc example (94 binaries) |
| fmt, clippy `-D warnings` | clean | clean |
| Strategy template and generator | did not exist | template built and its 4 tests passed; generator checks passed |
| TypeScript SDK | 103 tests passed | 248 tests passed; template scripts typecheck clean |

### Smoke swap

On devnet, `scripts/devnet/smoke.ts` passed with this wallet on Node 24.4.1 in 6 seconds.
It created a constant-product market, quoted 1,000,000 A to 1,993,980 B (4,927 CU) and swapped, and all five event checks passed.
Swap signature: [`5GC4aG6oEphMyrLng9bRb2NLqr3NNPKg1e3XezPSypi4fbyj6aqctZwRVCR6Ynz5ejWMjCSNVfs5nMTHxkvxNn3n`](https://explorer.solana.com/tx/5GC4aG6oEphMyrLng9bRb2NLqr3NNPKg1e3XezPSypi4fbyj6aqctZwRVCR6Ynz5ejWMjCSNVfs5nMTHxkvxNn3n?cluster=devnet) (35,478 CU, fee 2,500).
A run costs about 0.015 SOL.

On a local `solana-test-validator` 4.4.1, with the router and the example strategy loaded and this wallet as their upgrade authority, the same script passed in 126 s.
It also initialised the config and registered the strategy, and its swap was 35,488 CU.
It is slow there because every transaction waits for `finalized`.

### Quote timing

`pipeline-quoter` makes no network calls, so `scripts/quote-devnet` (a small tool in this repo) fetches the market, the strategy's bytecode, the accounts and the clock by RPC.
It then times the first quote and 10,000 warm ones.
It calls only `Quoter::quote`, never the BSL router's `simulate_swap`.

| Market | Strategy | RPC fetch | Resolve accounts | First quote | Warm mean, p50, p99 | Strategy CU |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `35H28SveyPAVr64VHYYZBif8cbhiXyALPghRxFZcVDSz` | example constant product | 391 ms | 2.8 ms | 188 µs | 139, 124, 343 µs | 4,902 |
| `2u5ep2aLFzp2SACkG5ZLUrAkEY7vCzm2vL56Q6YiQxb9` | outside builder `9mAV3p...` | 410 ms | 59 ms | 457 µs | 216, 195, 495 µs | 39,826 |

- Warm quotes take 100 to 220 µs on this 2017 Xeon, against the 10 to 20 µs in Pipeline's integrator guide.
- The same quote by RPC simulation through the TypeScript SDK took 21 ms warm and 229 ms cold, with the same output to the unit.
- Across all 44 devnet markets, 22 quote.
  - 18 of the 20 constant-product markets quote, 6 of them 0 out because their pools are lopsided. The other 2 fail with `AccountDidNotDeserialize`.
  - All 4 outside-builder markets quote.
  - None of the 12 bonding-curve markets quote: 9 fail with `WrongStatus` and 3 with `CannotFill`.
  - None of the 8 Pool4 markets quote: 6 fail with `AccountDidNotDeserialize` on `pool` and 2 with `CannotFill`.
  - RPC simulation fails the same way, so these failures are the markets' own state, not the quoter's.

### What broke

- **Node 26 against public devnet:** from the fifth WebSocket in a session, every connection fails (Node 26 runs WebSockets over HTTP/2, which it marks experimental). `@solana/kit` opens one per `sendAndConfirm`, so the smoke script failed at its sixth transaction even though the swap had landed. Node 24 has no such problem.
- **Platform tools v1.58** has no Intel macOS build, which is why the wrapper exists.
- **Faucets:** only Alchemy's airdrop works.
- **Public devnet throttles** with HTTP 429s and an occasional connect timeout. `quote-devnet` retries 429s.
- **Smoke script on Helius devnet:** it hung for over ten minutes after its first transaction. This was not diagnosed; use public devnet for the script.
- **Local validator:** the first airdrop, sent seconds after start, failed and the retries succeeded. A scratchpad-length ledger path is too long for the admin socket, which only adds log noise.
- **Downloads from GitHub** are flaky on this network. Auto mode also refused the Agave tarball download, so the owner ran the install script.

### For other tickets

Pipeline moved on after `a2d5bfb`. Three commits on 2026-11-09 added:

- `pipeline-check`, a conformance checker that trades a market through the real router in LiteSVM. It bears on [Canary checks on the four devnet strategies](/14/).
- Trust facts and a metadata standard in `pipeline-client`. These bear on [Explainer samples for the four devnet strategies](/15/).
- A strategy template with reproducible builds.
- A hosted devnet API at `https://pipeline-devnet.up.railway.app`. It indexes strategies, markets and swaps, and serves trust flags, quotes, swap transactions, trades, candles and a live stream. This bears on [Pipescope v1 scope](/3/) and [Pipescope architecture](/13/).

Devnet's router was redeployed at 21:00 UTC that day, and its bytes differ from the local builds.
macOS builds differ from Linux ones, though, so whether it matches `5ad130d` needs `solana-verify` 0.5.2 or later (this Mac has 0.4.9) and Docker. That has not been checked yet.

tickets.title: Where the quoter runs for Canary checks
tickets.decision: Canary checks run as native Rust on `litesvm` in a Cloudflare Container (about 35 MB; needs the $5 Workers Paid plan, an owner approval); WASM in a Worker is ruled out ([findings](/research/quoter-hosting/)).
tickets.resolution:
Findings: [quoter-hosting.md](/research/quoter-hosting/) (Pipeline at `a2d5bfb`, measured on this Mac against a live devnet market).

- **Cloudflare Container (native Rust, linux/amd64): works.** The quoter builds natively and ran the deployed router and the example constant-product strategy on market `LCHsnkMf...`: `Quoter::new` 15 to 18 ms, `quote` 160 µs, a buy `simulate_swap` 0.68 ms that matched the quote exactly, peak 33.6 MB resident. x86_64 keeps the sBPF JIT. Cold starts are "often 1-3 seconds" per Cloudflare's docs.
- **WASM in a Worker: ruled out.** It does not build (`blst`'s C code needs a wasm C compiler, and getrandom needs a flag). With those worked around it does not run: `std::time::Instant::now` panics in Agave's `process_message` through `solana-svm-measure`. Built for wasm32-wasip1 so the clock works, quotes run (217 µs), but the router swap fails with "Access violation ... in unallocated region" on the 32-bit host, so the exit test cannot run there.
- **Small server elsewhere: works, same binary.** Fly.io starts at $2.19 per 30 days, but it adds a second platform, a second home for the RPC key and an endpoint to guard.
- **Cost:** at 500 Canary runs a month (cold start, about 10 s of work, 2 min idle, `basic` 1/4 vCPU and 1 GiB), usage is about 18.5 GiB-hours of memory, under 45 vCPU-minutes and 74 GB-hours of disk, all inside the Workers Paid allowances. That means $0 on top of the **$5 a month Workers Paid subscription, which Containers require and which the owner must approve.**
- **Data from devnet:** the quoter never fetches data. Each run takes a snapshot of about ten RPC calls and about 0.9 MB (router and strategy ProgramData are most of it). That is roughly 5,000 Helius credits a month, against 1M free. Load the router from its deployed ProgramData. A strategy version is the program id plus the `slot` in its ProgramData header, so the indexer can queue a run when that slot changes. The public devnet RPC gave three 429s on one `getProgramAccounts`.
- **Design note:** `Quoter::simulate_swap` never commits state, and the quoter's `LiteSVM` is private. The exit test (buy, move the clock, sell) therefore needs a harness on `litesvm` directly, which has the same hosting needs.
- **Unverified:** a sell `simulate_swap` on devnet failed with router error 6002, which in `a2d5bfb` is `ListingFeeTooHigh`, so the deployed router probably differs from that source.

**Recommendation:** run the Canary runner as a native Rust binary (`litesvm` plus Pipeline's crates) in a Cloudflare Container on a `basic` instance, driven by Pipescope's Worker. Use one Durable Object per strategy version, and have the Worker build the snapshot so the container can run with `enableInternet = false`. Keep Fly.io as the fallback.

tickets.title: Which lending market the lending pool lends to
tickets.decision: Kamino Lend through its cToken deposit and redeem (no oracle or refresh, one call level spare inside a swap, live on devnet); Jupiter Lend only for keeper jobs ([findings](/research/lending-market/)).
tickets.resolution:
**Recommendation: Kamino Lend (klend), through its cToken instructions `deposit_reserve_liquidity` and `redeem_reserve_collateral`, never through obligations.**
Keep Jupiter Lend Earn as a possible second adapter for keeper jobs only.
MarginFi and Save are worse fits.

Decision-relevant facts:

- **Call depth inside a Pipeline swap** (limit is stack height 5 on devnet and mainnet): Kamino's redeem runs router 1, strategy 2, klend 3, SPL Token 4, so one level stays spare for a smart-wallet trader or an aggregator calling the router.
  Jupiter Lend's withdraw runs Lending 3, Liquidity 4, Token 5, so it uses the last level and fails with any extra outer level.
- **No refresh, no oracle:** Kamino's cToken deposit and redeem refresh the reserve themselves without a price (since at least 1.12.2), so the strategy passes 12 accounts and no oracle; Jupiter Lend needs no refresh either but takes 17 or 18 accounts.
  Kamino's obligation instructions refuse CPI from any program not on its 16-program whitelist (`CpiDisabled`), so obligations are out for us.
- **Compute (mainnet medians):** Kamino deposit 43.7k, redeem 29.7k; Jupiter Lend deposit 56.0k, withdraw 55.6k.
- **Near full utilisation:** Kamino refuses redeems above freely available liquidity (minus queued withdrawal tickets) and per-interval caps, and has a withdrawal queue; Jupiter Lend shares one slowly expanding withdrawal limit across all Earn depositors of a mint.
  Kamino's main SOL reserve was about 91% borrowed and USDC about 86% on 2026-11-09, so swaps above buffer plus withdrawable must fail cleanly whichever market we use.
- **Token-2022:** both accept Token-2022 lent mints only with no transfer hook and a zero transfer fee, so a contained token is never lent; we lend the SOL or USDC side.
- **Devnet:** klend is deployed on devnet at its mainnet id (last deploy 2026-09-01) and anyone can create a lending market and reserves, so the lending pool can have a devnet demo; Jupiter Lend's devnet programs date from July 2025 and its own guide says to test against cloned mainnet state.
- **Prior art:** Meteora's Dynamic Vault now lends only to Jupiter Lend, but it calls it at the top level, where the extra level costs nothing.
- **Correction:** `research/estimates.md` overstates the hooked-token call-depth problem; the lending call and the hooked token's transfer are sibling calls, so only Jupiter Lend's depth is a real limit.

Findings, with sources and commits: [lending-market.md](/research/lending-market/)

New questions for [Lending pool design](/21/) are listed at the end of that file (in-swap redeem or buffer only, which reserve, how cTokens are valued in the price, what to do near full utilisation or in Kamino emergency mode).

tickets.title: Where Pipescope's indexer gets its data
tickets.decision: port Top-pad's free-tier indexer: `logsSubscribe` on the router and strategy programs, reconciliation every minute, registry snapshots and a ProgramData watch; LaserStream is the paid mainnet upgrade ([findings](/research/indexer-data-source/)).
tickets.resolution:
Findings: [research/indexer-data-source.md](/research/indexer-data-source/) on branch `research/indexer-data-source` (Pipeline at `a2d5bfb`, Top-pad at `b833a7b`).

Decision-relevant facts:

- One address covers the router's whole life: every registration, market creation and swap through Pipeline is a router transaction, so trades need no per-market address list.
- Swap events are router self-CPI inner instructions, not log lines: a `logsSubscribe` notification only names the transaction, which must then be fetched (`getTransaction`) or streamed in full.
- The router never reports strategy upgrades (all four devnet strategies were redeployed on 2026-11-08 and the router on 2026-11-09 07:11 UTC, with no router event), custom actions such as adding liquidity, or bypass swaps; those need a watch on each strategy program and its ProgramData.
- The registry only grows (no router instruction closes a `Strategy` or `Market`), so a `getProgramAccounts` snapshot is a complete, history-free check of discovery.
- Devnet volume is tiny: 185 router transactions from 2026-11-07 18:30 to 2026-11-09 07:58 UTC (111 swaps, 42 markets, 4 strategies), about 5 an hour.
- Measured on 2026-11-09 (6 router transactions over 25 minutes): `logsSubscribe` notified about 1 s after block time and Helius free served each transaction 0.1 to 0.3 s later; the public devnet socket silently missed 1 of the 6, so reconciliation is required whatever the live source.
- Free tier on the shared Helius key: standard WebSockets and `getTransactionsForAddress` work on devnet; `transactionSubscribe` is refused ("not available on the free plan"); LaserStream needs Developer ($49 a month) for devnet and Business ($499) or Professional ($999) for mainnet, which Helius's pages disagree on.
- Webhooks: Helius documents retries two contradictory ways (24 hours with backoff, or 3 tries a second apart and then lost), and whether a raw payload carries inner instructions is unverified.
- Devnet history went back at least to 2025-04-23 on both Helius and the public endpoint, although Helius documents 2 weeks for devnet; devnet and Pipeline's devnet programs can be reset, so our own database is the record.
- Top-pad's indexer carries over almost whole: the idempotent entry point, cursor reconciliation, `logsSubscribe` parsing, `getBlock` positions, the Durable Object with its 15 s alarm and version reset, candles, and the restart test.

Recommendation: port Top-pad's free-tier indexer to Pipeline, watching the router and every registered strategy program over a standard `logsSubscribe` WebSocket on Helius devnet, decoding with Pipeline's SDK, reconciling from cursors every minute, snapshotting the registry and polling ProgramData for new strategy versions; about 400,000 Helius credits a month at today's volume, inside the free 1M.
LaserStream in a Cloudflare Container (48 hours of replay) is the paid upgrade for mainnet and is the owner's call; webhooks are not the primary source.

tickets.title: Prior art for behavioural testing of Solana programs
tickets.decision: no tool behaviour-tests Solana market programs; Canary copies EVM honeypot simulation and Jupiter's round-trip and quote-parity tests, adds acting as each authority then re-testing ([findings](/research/behavioural-testing-prior-art/)).
tickets.resolution:
Full findings, with a source for every fact: [research/behavioural-testing-prior-art.md](/research/behavioural-testing-prior-art/) on branch `research/behavioural-testing-prior-art` (Pipeline read at `a2d5bfb`).

### What we found

- Nothing tests an arbitrary Solana market program from outside.
  RugCheck, GoPlus (Solana), Birdeye, Webacy, Solsniffer, De.Fi and DexScreener read only mint, metadata and holder state; none simulates a sale on Solana, none looks at the pool program or its upgrade authority, and none publishes a false-positive rate.
  Birdeye says it outright: "There is no honeypot flag on Solana, because the equivalent danger is a live freeze authority."
- The nearest Solana prior art is Jupiter's: a $500 buy-then-sell round trip that every routed market must pass, re-checked every 30 minutes, and `jupiter-amm-test-kit`, which asserts in LiteSVM that the swap's token deltas equal the quote exactly (exact-in only, with the clock pinned to the snapshot).
- The closest analogue is EVM honeypot simulation.
  Honeypot.is buys and sells, replays sales from real holders, and reports buy, sell and transfer tax.
  HoneyCheck (arXiv 2610.10149, October 2026) buys, waits, then sells.
  Waiting up to 10 seconds caught 191 honeypots that an immediate sale missed.
  Replaying from allowlisted insider wallets found 4,039 addresses that could sell when fresh wallets could not.
  It flagged none of 967 benign tokens and agreed with 90.2% of labelled honeypots, against 87.1% for Honeypot.is and 59.6% for GoPlus.
- Every simulator reviewed tests only the present state, and has the same blind spots: a block added after purchase (a later blacklist, fee change or upgrade), and code that detects simulation (Blowfish's `RELIABLE_SIMULATION_NOT_POSSIBLE`, X-ray's `MaliciousSimulation` rule).
  False positives are rare and come from benign mechanisms (anti-bot code, cooldowns, presale locks); most errors are false negatives.
- Upgrades: OtterSec's verified-build registry un-verifies a program when it sees an upgrade (webhook plus a poll about every 5 minutes); no tool found re-runs a behavioural test per program version, so Canary's per-version rule has no precedent.
- Pipeline facts that shape the harness:
  - The router already blocks a hostile strategy's attempts to take more than the trader sent, steal fees or re-enter, so Canary need not retest those.
  - `Quoter::simulate_swap` uses a fresh wallet each call and never commits state, so a buy-then-sell test needs its own harness that commits the buy.
  - The quoter's LiteSVM runs with signature checks off, so a harness built the same way can act as any authority.

### Recommendation: what Canary checks should add

- **Exit test**:
  - A committed buy-then-sell round trip on the same wallet.
  - Several fresh wallets plus the insiders (creator, upgrade authority, custom-action signers); any difference between the two groups is a finding.
  - A size ladder starting at 0.1% of liquidity; report the largest sale that works.
  - A time ladder from the same slot out to one epoch.
  - Sales of tokens that arrived by plain transfer.
  - A stated cause for every failure (strategy, token, missing fee account or compute).
- **Quote against swap**: exact equality between the quote and the router-measured swap, in both directions, across the size ladder, for exact-out where supported, and at more than one clock time; report quotes over the 200,000-unit cap.
- **Fee honesty**:
  - Split realised cost into the Pipeline fee, the integrator fee, the Token-2022 transfer fee and the strategy's own part.
  - Measure buy and sell separately, per wallet and over time.
  - Check again after the authorities have used their powers.
- **Control**:
  - Program: upgradeable or frozen, the type of upgrade authority, the program hash as the strategy version, and whether a verified build exists.
  - Mints: their authorities and Token-2022 extensions.
  - Act as each authority, call each custom action, then re-run the exit test and fee honesty; this closes the later-blacklist gap the EVM tools leave open.
  - Bypass: call the strategy directly, without the router.
  - Flag strategies that read transaction-context sysvars.
- **Re-run** on every upgrade (watch the loader and poll `ProgramData.slot`), on mint authority or extension changes, on `MetadataUpdated`, and on a schedule; each result is scoped to a slot and a program hash.

tickets.title: Pool4 maths on a single Pipeline strategy, and what MetalLegBob's pool4.json strategy is
tickets.decision: Pool4 fits one strategy (the buy wall as a second curve segment, trim and cap ratchet as bookkeeping after pricing); `pool4.json` is MetalLegBob's own closed-source Pool4 port ([findings](/research/pool4-on-pipeline/)).
tickets.resolution:
Findings: [pool4-on-pipeline.md](/research/pool4-on-pipeline/) (branch `research/pool4-on-pipeline`, not for merging).

**Does Pool4 fit one strategy whose quote and swap share code? Yes.**

- Pricing is a two-segment curve: the full-range constant product, plus the buy wall as a SOL-only segment from its top down to almost zero (that is how IMD's `CappedBurnHook` places it). It is bounded at two steps, needs no square root and no tick arrays in the swap, and needs no account beyond the output vault if the wall's SOL sits in the quote vault.
- The trim and the cap ratchet (with its floor and daily decay) run inside `pipeline_swap` *after* the output is priced, as bookkeeping in the market state. They never change the quote, move no tokens, and keep the input in the input vault as Pipeline asks.
- Burning and paying out the trimmed tokens, placing the wall, and sweeping fees are keeper jobs (custom actions).
- Pipeline-specific rule: pass the vault's full booked total (reserves plus every ledger) to `credited_input`, or Token-2022 transfer fees make the books drift.
- If any time-based change runs before pricing, the quote depends on the clock. Keep every time-based change after pricing.

**Compute** (measured on devnet in MetalLegBob's port):

- Buy, including the ratchet: 15.4k to 16.7k units.
- Sell, including a trim: 12.9k to 14.2k.
- Sell that fills the wall: 28.6k.
- For comparison, Pipeline's example constant-product strategy: 8.8k to 12.0k.
- Keeper jobs: placing the wall 10.8k, settling the burn 15.6k, sweeping fees 20.3k.
- All of these are far under the quoter's 200k cap.

**What `pool4.json` (`4ajWF6Y3...`) is:** MetalLegBob's own Pool4 port, not a four-mint pool. The census label in `research/pipeline-router.md` is wrong.

- Each market has 2 mints (a Token-2022 token and wSOL), trades exact-in only, and is created when a token graduates from his bonding-curve strategy through `pipeline_seed_liquidity`.
- Fees: 50 bps of the input to a fee ledger that a keeper sweeps, plus 15 bps in SOL kept by the pool.
- It trims to the inventory cap at an unchanged price, and the cap decays at 0.1% of the seeded inventory a day.
- It has a SOL buy wall that bought tokens on devnet, placed by `RebalanceWall` behind a reference-price guard.
- `SettleRetired` burns the trimmed tokens. The keeper tip is 0.22% of the work.
- The source is not public, the metadata is a placeholder, and he registered it on 2026-11-08. Several of these facts are inferred from replaying the market's trades; the file marks which.

tickets.title: How the containment hook works with the router and unlocks
tickets.decision: allow only the home market's vault and its `["fees", market]` account; a permissionless PDA-signed `unlock` clears the hook program and its authority; the tax AMM's market state counts the volume ([findings](/research/containment-hook-mechanics/)).
tickets.resolution:
Findings: [containment-hook-mechanics.md](/research/containment-hook-mechanics/)
Read from Pipeline `a2d5bfb`, the Factory's hook at `da2529b`, Token-2022 at `486240c` and the owner's Jupiter and Meteora knowledge base; nothing was sent on chain.

**Accounts the hook must allow**
- Two per home market: the home market's vault for the contained mint, and the market's Pipeline fee account for that mint (the associated token account of `["fees", market]`). Without the fee account, buys work and sells fail, as Pipeline's own test shows.
- The treasury needs no entry: `sweep_fees` moves tokens out of the fee account, and that side is already allowed.
- Integrator fee accounts matter only for an integrator fee on a sell, which the router takes in the contained token. With a zero rate the router makes no transfer at all. If they are allowed, it must be as destinations only, from a list the launcher sets. Allowed as sources too, they become a way out to a vamp.
- With allowed sources limited to accounts that programs move (the vault by the strategy, the fee account by `sweep_fees`), every transfer touches the home market, so tokens held anywhere else can only go back into it.
- Pipeline's `test-hook` approves everything when its extra accounts are left out, and Token-2022 does call hooks without them, so its allowlist can be skipped. Build on the Factory's fail-closed pattern instead: every account required, the `transferring` check, no CPI.

**Unlock**
- Make the mint's transfer-hook authority a PDA of the hook program. A permissionless `unlock` checks the goal, then signs `TransferHookInstruction::Update(None)` and `SetAuthority(TransferHookProgramId, None)`.
- Clear both fields. Meteora's DAMM v2 and DLMM accept a hooked mint permissionlessly only when both are unset, and DBC clears both at graduation.
- After the unlock nothing changes for the router or integrators: Token-2022 skips null hooks, and leftover hook accounts are ignored. Jupiter routed 4 of 4 graduated DBC hook mints.
- The hook program must be frozen before mainnet, because its upgrade authority could otherwise rewrite the rules.

**Volume**
- No program can read the swap event, which is an inner self-CPI. The router's `Market` account holds no volume, and anyone can empty the fee account (through `sweep_fees`) or send tokens into it.
- Counting in the hook works for any strategy, but it also counts liquidity moves and donations, and it write-locks a shared account on every transfer.

**Recommendation:** our tax AMM counts the quote-side volume of router swaps (calls signed by the market signer) in its market state, and the hook's `unlock` reads that account. v1 supports home markets on our tax AMM only.

tickets.title: Prior art for AI explanations of contracts, and what an explainer can safely say
tickets.decision: the explainer narrates only a Pipescope-built fact table and Canary results, every claim cites an evidence id checked in code, metadata stays untrusted author text, never verdicts ([findings](/research/explainer-prior-art/)).
tickets.resolution:
Full findings, with a source for every fact: [explainer-prior-art.md](/research/explainer-prior-art/) (branch `research/explainer-prior-art`, Pipeline read at `a2d5bfb`).

### What others do

- Nobody found ships an LLM explanation of a market program to traders at the point of trade on Solana.
  The nearest are Jupiter's AI Token Summary (project-level), Etherscan's contract-review skill (developer-facing, "not a security audit or safety certification") and per-transaction explainers (Helius Orb, Blockscout).
- Wallet tools at signing time (MetaMask with Blockaid, Rabby, Phantom, Jupiter Shield) use simulation and rules with short fixed labels and severity levels, not LLM prose.
- Those that use an LLM keep it accurate the same way: deterministic facts first, the model narrates only from them, a source on every claim, confirmed, inferred and unknown kept apart, and the date and version shown (Etherscan's skill; Blockscout uses an LLM only when its algorithms cannot classify; MATEX's research shows an auditing step and provenance lift faithfulness from 51 to 73).
- Wording consensus: labelled AI-generated and possibly wrong (Jupiter: "may contain inaccuracies ... Neither constitutes financial advice"), never an audit or a safety rating, neutral facts not verdicts, creator text marked unverified, feedback on every summary.
- Pipeline's integrator guide asks for "neutral facts and no judgements"; the router stores any metadata URI unvalidated (audit test H053 stores a `javascript:` string with a right-to-left override) and the author can change it at any time, even while the router is paused, without an upgrade.

### Recommendation

- **Inputs**: a numbered fact table built by Pipescope (strategy version hash, upgrade authority or frozen, market and mint facts, Token-2022 extensions, vault balances, age, volume), Canary results per version with dates, verified-build status from `solana-verify`, source excerpts only when the build matches the deployed hash, the canonical IDL from the Program Metadata program, and Pipeline's fixed rules; strategy metadata only as attributed, untrusted author text, with action discriminators cross-checked in code.
- **Shape**: the facts panel is rendered by our code, never by the model; the explainer is a tool-less narration beside it, generated once per strategy version, metadata hash and Canary run, cached, and regenerated on upgrade or `MetadataUpdated`; every generation is a paid call the owner approves.
- **Output contract**: structured claims, each `confirmed` or `inferred` with evidence ids from the fact table; code rejects claims without valid ids, numbers not in their evidence, URLs, Markdown or HTML, and banned terms (safe, audited, scam, rug, recommended, buy or sell advice, and similar); render as escaped plain text; fall back to facts only.
  Use our own evidence ids, not the provider's citations feature: on the Claude API citations and structured outputs cannot be combined.
- **Wording**: describe what the code and accounts allow, never intent; Canary passes reported as observed, scoped and dated, never as promises; author text attributed; say that router protections cover swaps only and custom actions are signed directly; a fixed UI label (sample for #15: "Written by an AI from this strategy version's code, on-chain data and Canary results on <date>. It can be wrong. It is not an audit, a safety rating or advice.") and a "this is wrong" control.
- **Prompt injection** (OWASP LLM01 and LLM05:2025, Anthropic's guidance, Beurer-Kellner et al. 2025): no tools or secrets in the explainer call; untrusted text normalised in code (control and bidirectional characters stripped, lengths capped, linked URLs never fetched), JSON-encoded and labelled with its origin in a tool result; a policy in the system prompt to report embedded instructions as a fact; a hostile-metadata fixture set run in CI; a second model screen only with the owner's approval, since it doubles paid calls.

### Effects on other tickets

- #15: build samples from this fact table and output contract, include one hostile-metadata sample, pick a model with structured outputs.
- #14: Canary results must be machine-readable records (check, strategy version, date, inputs, result), with a control result listing every non-Pipeline instruction and who may call it.
- #3: the explainer runs once per strategy version and metadata change, cached; the facts panel stays separate; add the feedback control.
- #13: a job reacting to upgrades and `MetadataUpdated`, running `solana-verify` on devnet and fetching metadata with size limits.
- #4: our own strategies publish verified builds, a canonical IDL and complete metadata.

pipeline.finding: Since the 2026-11-08 21:10 UTC upgrades, 6 of the Pool4 port's 8 markets and 2 of the constant product's 20 fail every quote and swap (`AccountDidNotDeserialize`); nothing the router emits says so.

The router never reports strategy upgrades (all four devnet strategies were redeployed on 2026-11-08 and the router on 2026-11-09 07:11 UTC, with no router event), custom actions such as adding liquidity, or bypass swaps; those need a watch on each strategy program and its ProgramData.

**Call depth inside a Pipeline swap** (limit is stack height 5 on devnet and mainnet): Kamino's redeem runs router 1, strategy 2, klend 3, SPL Token 4, so one level stays spare for a smart-wallet trader or an aggregator calling the router. Jupiter Lend's withdraw runs Lending 3, Liquidity 4, Token 5, so it uses the last level and fails with any extra outer level.

**WASM in a Worker: ruled out.** It does not build (`blst`'s C code needs a wasm C compiler, and getrandom needs a flag). With those worked around it does not run: `std::time::Instant::now` panics in Agave's `process_message` through `solana-svm-measure`. Built for wasm32-wasip1 so the clock works, quotes run (217 µs), but the router swap fails with "Access violation ... in unallocated region" on the 32-bit host, so the exit test cannot run there.

**Node 26 against public devnet:** from the fifth WebSocket in a session, every connection fails (Node 26 runs WebSockets over HTTP/2, which it marks experimental). `@solana/kit` opens one per `sendAndConfirm`, so the smoke script failed at its sixth transaction even though the swap had landed. Node 24 has no such problem.
`sh -c "$(curl -sSfL https://release.anza.xyz/v4.4.1/install)"` (in Pipeline's `docs/DEVNET.md`) switches agave-install's `active_release`, and with it the `solana` every project uses.

documents.title: Toolchain
documents.body:
What this project builds, tests and runs Pipeline with, and the steps that work.
Verified on 2026-11-09 against Pipeline commit `a2d5bfb`, and on 2026-11-10 against `5ad130d` (its newest), on the owner's Mac (iMac Pro, Intel Xeon W-2150B, x86_64, 10 cores, 32 GB, macOS 15.7.3), from [Run Pipeline on this Mac and on devnet](/2/).
Build tickets start here.

## Versions

| Tool | Version | Where it lives | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rust (host) | 1.97.1 | rustup toolchain `1.97.1` | Pipeline's `rust-toolchain.toml` selects it |
| cargo-build-sbf | 4.6.0 | `~/.local/share/testing-pipeline/toolchain/cargo-build-sbf-4.6.0/bin` | sBPF v3 output; Pipeline's CI pins it |
| Platform tools | v1.57 on Intel macOS, v1.58 elsewhere (rustc 1.95.0, clang 22.1.2) | `~/.cache/solana/v1.57` | v1.58, 4.6.0's default and Pipeline's pin, ships no Intel macOS build |
| Agave CLI | 4.4.1 | `~/.local/share/testing-pipeline/toolchain/agave-v4.4.1/bin` | `solana-test-validator` for local runs; Pipeline's docs name 4.4 |
| Node | 24.4.1 (nvm) | `~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.4.1` | Node 26 breaks WebSocket confirmations on public devnet (see Known problems) |
