| TypeScript SDK | `@solana/kit` 8.6.0, `@solana-program/token` 0.18.0, `@solana-program/system` 0.16.0, TypeScript 7.0.2 | each package's `node_modules` | from Pipeline's lockfiles |
| LiteSVM | 0.18.2 | Cargo | pinned by `pipeline-quoter` |

The machine's own defaults stay as they were, because the owner's other projects use them:

- Solana CLI 2.2.20 through agave-install's `active_release`, with its cargo-build-sbf 2.2.20 and platform tools v1.48 linked as the rustup toolchain `solana`.
- Default Node 26.9.0 (`~/.local/bin/node`) and default Rust `stable` 1.88.0.

## Install

```sh
bash scripts/install-toolchain.sh      # once per machine; safe to run again
source scripts/toolchain-env.sh        # in every shell (and every agent Bash call) that needs it
```

The install script puts Rust 1.97.1, cargo-build-sbf 4.6.0, the platform tools and the Agave 4.4.1 release side by side under `~/.local/share/testing-pipeline/toolchain` (override with `TESTING_PIPELINE_TOOLCHAIN`).
It checks the Agave tarball against the SHA-256 digest GitHub publishes for the release asset.
The env file puts those first on `PATH` for the current shell only, sets `SBF_TOOLS_VERSION` for this host, and puts Node 24 first when nvm has it.
On Intel macOS it also puts a small `cargo-build-sbf` wrapper first (`~/.local/share/testing-pipeline/toolchain/shims`, written by the install script) that adds `--tools-version v1.57` unless the caller passes one.
cargo-build-sbf takes the platform tools version only from that flag or from `[workspace.metadata.solana] tools-version` in the workspace's `Cargo.toml`, which Pipeline pins to v1.58 since `5ad130d`, and Pipeline's own scripts and strategy template call a bare `cargo build-sbf`; without the wrapper they would ask for v1.58, which cannot be installed on this Mac.
The explicit flag wins over the workspace pin: every build at `5ad130d` went through the wrapper on v1.57.
After the owner ran the script on 2026-11-10, `solana --version` outside the env file still printed 2.2.20, agave-install's `active_release` still pointed at 2.2.20, and rustup still had both the `solana` and `1.95.0-sbpf-solana-v1.57` links.

Two commands from Pipeline's own docs would change every project on the machine, so never run them as written:

- `cargo install cargo-build-sbf --version 4.6.0 --locked` without `--root` puts it in `~/.cargo/bin`, which cargo searches before `PATH`, so every project's `cargo build-sbf` would become 4.6.0.
- `sh -c "$(curl -sSfL https://release.anza.xyz/v4.4.1/install)"` (in Pipeline's `docs/DEVNET.md`) switches agave-install's `active_release`, and with it the `solana` every project uses.

### How the two cargo-build-sbf versions share rustup

On its first run cargo-build-sbf 4.6.0 uninstalls rustup's `solana` toolchain link and links its own, `1.95.0-sbpf-solana-v1.57`.
cargo-build-sbf 2.2.20 only looks at toolchains whose name starts with `solana` and relinks its own when it is missing, and 4.6.0 stops at its own link (which rustup lists first), so after the first run the two leave each other alone.
The install script restores the `solana` link anyway.
Checked by building a small program with 2.2.20, then 4.6.0, then listing the links: both builds passed and both links stayed.

## Build and test Pipeline

Clone Pipeline into a scratchpad, never into this repo, and note the commit.

These are the steps of Pipeline's CI at `5ad130d` (at `a2d5bfb`, before `scripts/build-programs.sh` and the strategy template existed, the programs were built with one `(cd programs && cargo build-sbf)`):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/MetalLegBob/pipeline.git && cd pipeline && git log -1 --format=%h
source <this repo>/scripts/toolchain-env.sh
export CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0

scripts/build-programs.sh            # each program on its own, as solana-verify builds them
cargo fmt --all -- --check && (cd programs && cargo fmt --all -- --check)
cargo test --workspace               # LiteSVM
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
scripts/test-template.sh             # builds and tests templates/strategy against these sources
scripts/test-new-strategy.sh
(cd sdk/ts && npm ci && npm run build && npm test)
(cd templates/strategy/scripts && npm ci && npm run typecheck)
```

| Step | `a2d5bfb` (2026-11-09) | `5ad130d` (2026-11-10) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build the programs | 5 programs, sBPF v3 (ELF `e_flags` 3): `pipeline.so` 401,816 bytes, `test_strategy_cp.so` 250,792, `test_strategy_evil.so` 92,208, `test_hook_refill.so` 28,360, `test_hook.so` 25,488; 37 s from clean | the same 5, one at a time: `pipeline.so` 402,544, `test_strategy_cp.so` 250,312, the rest unchanged; 52 s |
| `cargo fmt --check` | both workspaces clean | both workspaces clean |
| `cargo test --workspace` | 425 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored, in 82 test binaries; 399 s from clean, mostly compiling | 464 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (a doc example in `pipeline-check`), in 94 test binaries; 226 s on top of the earlier build |
| `cargo clippy -D warnings` | clean, 38 s | clean, 17 s |
| Strategy template, generator | did not exist | template built and its 4 tests passed (including one that runs `pipeline-check` on a Token-2022 transfer-fee market), 144 s; generator checks passed |
| TypeScript | SDK: typecheck and Prettier clean, 103 tests in 8 files, 2.4 s | SDK: 248 tests in 14 files, 13 s with `npm ci`; template scripts typecheck clean |

`cargo build-sbf` warns that each program declares both `cdylib` and `lib` crate types, which turns off LTO; that is Pipeline's choice and harmless here.

### Pipeline after `a2d5bfb`

Three commits on 2026-11-09 between 20:18 and 22:21 UTC added pieces that overlap this project's products:

- `crates/pipeline-check`, a conformance checker that quotes and trades a market through the real router in LiteSVM, from a strategy's own tests or against a deployed market (`pipeline-check --url devnet --market <MARKET>`), reporting Pass, Warn, Fail or Skip per check.
- Trust facts and a metadata standard in `pipeline-client` (`facts.rs`, `metadata.rs`).
- A strategy template (`templates/strategy`, `scripts/new-strategy.sh`) and reproducible builds with `solana-verify` (`docs/VERIFICATION.md`); `pipeline-strategy-interface` moved from `crates/` to `programs/`.
- A hosted devnet API, `https://pipeline-devnet.up.railway.app` (`docs/API.md`): strategies and markets with trust flags, quotes, unsigned swap transactions, trades, candles and a live event stream, with no keys and per-IP limits.

Devnet's router was redeployed at 21:00 UTC that day (slot 520,510,501).
Its bytes differ from both local builds, which proves nothing: Pipeline's `docs/VERIFICATION.md` says macOS builds differ from Linux ones and makes the Docker build the reference.
Checking which commit devnet runs needs `solana-verify` 0.5.2 or later (this Mac has 0.4.9 in `~/.avm/bin`) and Docker Desktop running; not done yet.
`scripts/quote-devnet` stays pinned to `a2d5bfb`'s crates, where its timings were measured.

## Devnet

### Wallet

This project's devnet wallet is `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/wallet.json` (mode 600, directory 700), public key `9rYtQM57An5FRiVMkE5aZVRMtq5i1uwN3iiAEjRoywCt`.
It is never committed, and this project does not use Top-pad's (Heat's) devnet bank.
Pass it explicitly: `-k ~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/wallet.json` to the Solana CLI, `KEYPAIR=...` to Pipeline's scripts.

Fund it from the CLI, never through a web faucet (owner, 2026-11-10), with the owner's machine-wide `devnet-airdrop` (in `~/.local/bin`, not in this repo), started in the background:

```sh
devnet-airdrop ~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/wallet.json --target 12
```

It pulls 1 SOL per request from Alchemy's devnet RPC (key `ALCHEMY_API_KEY` in the shared env file; free tier, so not a paid call), a few per burst, and repeats every 15 minutes until the target.
That is how this wallet went from 1.94 to 12.94 SOL on 2026-11-10: eleven 1 SOL airdrops from Alchemy between 01:25 and 02:18 UTC, two or three per round.
What did not work, on 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-10:

- `solana airdrop` on public devnet: rate-limited from the first request, and now closed (HTTP 410).
- Helius devnet RPC's airdrop: rate-limited, then HTTP 500.
- `devnet-pow` (installed in `~/.cargo/bin`): every proof-of-work faucet on devnet was empty.

Spend devnet SOL only on real devnet transactions and deployments; local runs use `solana-test-validator` or LiteSVM, where SOL is free.

### RPC

Public devnet (`https://api.devnet.solana.com`) with Node 24 is what works for Pipeline's scripts.
Devnet now finalizes in about a second: each of the smoke script's six transactions, confirmed at `finalized`, landed one second after the last.

### Smoke swap

```sh
(cd sdk/ts && npm ci && npm run build)
cd scripts/devnet && npm ci
RPC_URL=https://api.devnet.solana.com KEYPAIR=$HOME/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/wallet.json node smoke.ts
```

Passed with Node 24.4.1 in 6 seconds: two fresh mints, a constant-product market and its fee accounts, liquidity, account resolution, a quote by RPC simulation (1,000,000 A to 1,993,980 B, 4,927 CU), the swap, and all five event checks (output equals the quote, `net_sent` equals the input, fee 2,500 is 0.25% rounded up, the market matches).
Swap signature: [`5GC4aG6oEphMyrLng9bRb2NLqr3NNPKg1e3XezPSypi4fbyj6aqctZwRVCR6Ynz5ejWMjCSNVfs5nMTHxkvxNn3n`](https://explorer.solana.com/tx/5GC4aG6oEphMyrLng9bRb2NLqr3NNPKg1e3XezPSypi4fbyj6aqctZwRVCR6Ynz5ejWMjCSNVfs5nMTHxkvxNn3n?cluster=devnet) (35,478 CU).
A run costs about 0.015 devnet SOL.

### Quoting with pipeline-quoter

`pipeline-quoter` never touches the network, so `scripts/quote-devnet` feeds it from RPC: it lists the router's markets, or fetches one market, its strategy's bytecode, the accounts the trade reads and the clock, resolves the strategy's accounts, then times the first quote and 10,000 warm quotes.
It takes Pipeline's crates from Pipeline's repository at `a2d5bfb` and calls only `Quoter::quote`, never `simulate_swap`, which runs the BSL-licensed router.

```sh
cd scripts/quote-devnet
cargo run --release -- https://api.devnet.solana.com list
cargo run --release -- https://api.devnet.solana.com <MARKET> [AMOUNT] [INPUT_INDEX] [OUTPUT_INDEX]
```

On this Mac, quoting 1,000,000 units of mint 0 into mint 1:

| Market | Strategy | Fetch (RPC) | Load program | Resolve | First quote | Warm quote mean, p50, p99 | Strategy CU |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `35H28SveyPAVr64VHYYZBif8cbhiXyALPghRxFZcVDSz` | constant product `yRptCd...` | 391 ms, 3 calls | 2.1 ms | 2.8 ms | 188 us | 139, 124, 343 us | 4,902 |
| `2u5ep2aLFzp2SACkG5ZLUrAkEY7vCzm2vL56Q6YiQxb9` | outside builder `9mAV3p...` | 410 ms, 4 calls | 8.6 ms | 59 ms (one RPC round) | 457 us | 216, 195, 495 us | 39,826 |

Warm quotes take about 100 to 220 microseconds on this 2017 Xeon, against the 10 to 20 microseconds Pipeline's integrator guide quotes; a market's first quote costs a few hundred milliseconds of RPC, then nothing more while its accounts stay cached.
The same quote by RPC simulation through the TypeScript SDK (`quoteStrategy`) took 21 ms on a warm connection and 229 ms on a cold one, plus 36 to 286 ms to resolve accounts, and several seconds or connect timeouts while public devnet was throttling.
Both ways gave the same output to the unit (6,946,345,550,466 and 1,993,940); the SDK reports about 25 more compute units because it counts the whole simulated transaction.

Of the 44 markets on devnet at 08:45 UTC, quoting 1,000,000 units of mint 0 into mint 1:

| Strategy | Markets | Quote | Do not quote |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Constant product (example) `yRptCd...` | 20 | 18 (6 of them quote 0 out: their pools are so lopsided, such as 763 trillion units of A against 210 million of B, that the input is worth less than one unit out) | 2: `AccountDidNotDeserialize` (3003) on the `pool` account during account resolution |
| Outside builder `9mAV3p...` | 4 | 4 | none |
| Bonding curve `ETrmUe...` | 12 | none | 9 `WrongStatus` (6004, "Not allowed in the curve's current status"), 3 `CannotFill` (6006, "The curve cannot fill that trade") |
| Pool4 `4ajWF6...` | 8 | none | 6 `AccountDidNotDeserialize` (3003) on `pool` during account resolution, 2 `CannotFill` (6006, "The pool cannot fill that trade") |

RPC simulation through the SDK fails the same way, so these are the markets' own states, not the quoter.
`AccountDidNotDeserialize` on `pool` suggests markets created by an older version of the strategy program, whose state the upgraded program can no longer read.

## Local validator

Pipeline's `docs/DEVNET.md` gives the command, adapted here to this project's wallet (the programs' upgrade authority, so the script initialises the router's config and registers the example strategy itself) and a ledger outside the clone:

```sh
source <this repo>/scripts/toolchain-env.sh
ME=$(solana-keygen pubkey ~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/wallet.json)
solana-test-validator --reset --ledger <scratchpad>/test-ledger \
  --deactivate-feature 6TkHkRmP7JZy1fdM6fg5uXn76wChQBWGokHBJzrLB3mj \
  --upgradeable-program PiPEf4fFBpYXCtgfiWgVWzZNXnq2wZ7bnXidJCTwf34 programs/target/deploy/pipeline.so $ME \
  --upgradeable-program yRptCdde1du1JYR2DcNFtLC1fkp5Asd6rE3XSvZoUFx programs/target/deploy/test_strategy_cp.so $ME
# in another shell (agents: start the validator with run_in_background, stop it with TaskStop)
solana -u localhost airdrop 100 $ME
cd scripts/devnet && RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8899 KEYPAIR=~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/wallet.json node smoke.ts
```

`--deactivate-feature` switches off SIMD-0268's deeper call limit, which test validators turn on by default but devnet and mainnet do not have yet.

Passed on 2026-11-10 with `solana-test-validator` 4.4.1 and Node 24.4.1, in 126 seconds: config initialised (listing fee 0.01 SOL), strategy registered, market created and funded, quote 1,000,000 A to 1,993,980 B (4,929 CU), the swap (35,488 CU, fee 2,500) and all five event checks.
It is slower than devnet because the script confirms every transaction at `finalized`, which a fresh local validator reaches only after about 32 slots of 400 ms each.
Two things to know:

- The first airdrop, sent seconds after the validator came up, failed with "airdrop request failed"; the same request a few seconds later, and every one after it, went through.
- With a ledger path longer than macOS's 104-character socket limit (any scratchpad path), the validator logs `Unable to start admin rpc service: path must be shorter than SUN_LEN` and its terminal dashboard repeats `admin.rpc does not exist`; RPC, the faucet and the programs work regardless, so it is noise.

## Known problems

- **Node 26 and public devnet WebSockets.**
  Node 26.9.0 opens WebSockets over HTTP/2, which it marks experimental, and against `wss://api.devnet.solana.com` the fifth and every later connection on the same session fails at once (Node 24 opened ten in a row).
  `@solana/kit` opens a connection per `sendAndConfirm`, so Pipeline's smoke script failed with `SolanaError: WebSocket failed to connect` at its sixth transaction, the swap, which had landed anyway.
  Use Node 24 (`scripts/toolchain-env.sh` does) until this is fixed; Helius devnet WebSockets did not show it.
- **Public devnet throttles.**
  Once, Node 24 timed out connecting to `api.devnet.solana.com` mid-run, and sweeping all 44 markets drew HTTP 429s; `quote-devnet` retries 429s with back-off.
- **Helius devnet and the smoke script.**
  With `RPC_URL` and `WS_URL` on Helius devnet, the script sent its first transaction, which landed, and then waited for its confirmation for over ten minutes before it was stopped; not diagnosed, so use public devnet for the script.
- **Platform tools v1.58 has no Intel macOS build**, so on this Mac `cargo build-sbf` must run on v1.57, which has the same Rust (1.95.0) and builds sBPF v3; the wrapper `toolchain-env.sh` puts first does this (see Install).
- **Downloads from GitHub are flaky on this network**: `gh` calls hit TLS timeouts and connection resets; retry.

documents.title: Spec
documents.body:
The build-ready spec for the Pipeline suite on devnet, charted by Map: a build-ready spec for the Pipeline suite on devnet.
This file holds what every product shares; each product has its own file beside it, and decisions with a lasting trade-off are ADRs in `docs/adr/`.
Terms are as in `GLOSSARY.md`, and the toolchain and its install steps are in `docs/toolchain.md`.

## Product files

- `pipescope.md`: Aviary's first devnet version.
- `pipescope-architecture.md`: where each part of Aviary runs and keeps its data.
- `pipescope-canary.md`: Aviary's Canary checks.
- `pipescope-explainer.md`: Aviary's explainer.
- `tax-amm.md`: the tax AMM.
- `containment-hook.md`: the containment hook.
- `pool4-for-solana.md`: the buy wall AMM.
- `lending-pool.md`: the lending AMM.

The files keep the names they were written under, so links to them still work; "Names" below says what each product is called.

## Names

- The suite and its terminal share one public name, **Aviary**.
- Our on-chain products keep plain descriptive names and carry the suite's name before their own in public: Aviary Tax AMM, Aviary Containment Hook, Aviary Buy Wall AMM and Aviary Lending AMM.
  In prose they are the tax AMM, the containment hook, the buy wall AMM and the lending AMM.
- Canary checks keep their name; they are a feature of Aviary, with no address or handle of their own.
- The buy wall AMM is a port of IMD's Pool4 design and says so wherever it is described; Pool4 is IMD's product name and is never part of ours.
- Aviary's address is `aviary.trade` and its X handle is `@aviarytrade`.
  The owner registers both, and nothing links to either until it exists.
- A name is cheap to change, because each lives in one place:
  - the terminal's public name, address and fee label are one config module of the web app (`pipescope-architecture.md`, "`terminal-web`");
  - each on-chain program's public name lives beside the program and nowhere else: the `name` in its strategy metadata, and the `name` in the `security.txt` it embeds, a build-time constant.
- Nothing else in code carries a public name: apps, packages, Workers, databases, crates and programs are named for what they are (`terminal-web`, `tax-amm`, `containment-hook`, `buy-wall-amm`, `lending-amm`).
- The repo and folder keep the internal name `testing-pipeline`.

## Our products live inside Aviary

Decided with the owner in [Pipescope v1 scope](/3/).

- The tax AMM, the containment hook, the buy wall AMM and the lending AMM get no websites of their own.
- Their user actions run through Aviary's custom-action forms, from each strategy's own complete metadata (see "Metadata, IDL and conformance report" below).
- Each product adds its own panel and forms to Aviary when it is built, for example progress toward the unlock goal for the containment hook, the wall and the inventory cap for the buy wall AMM, the buffer for the lending AMM, and the launch form and payouts that `tax-amm.md` describes for the tax AMM.
- So each product's build tickets include its metadata, its Aviary panel and its Aviary forms.

## Engineering and security bar for on-chain programs

Decided with the owner on 2026-11-10 in [Engineering and security bar for our on-chain programs](/4/), against Pipeline commit `5ad130d`.
It applies to every on-chain program we write: the tax AMM, the containment hook, the buy wall AMM, the lending AMM and any single-use AMM.
A program's build tickets count as done on devnet only when the program meets all of it, and each build ticket's acceptance criteria name the sections below that it covers.
External audits belong to the mainnet launch effort, which is out of scope.

### Framework and toolchain

- Anchor `=1.2.2`, with the rest pinned as Pipeline pins it: Rust 1.97.1, cargo-build-sbf 4.6.0, platform tools v1.58 (v1.57 on the owner's Intel Mac, see `docs/toolchain.md`), sBPF v3, LiteSVM 0.18.2 and Kani 0.67.0.
- When Pipeline moves a pin, we move ours to match, in a PR of its own; Anchor 2.0 waits for a stable release and for Pipeline to move.
- Native code or Pinocchio only when a build ticket measures that a program cannot fit its compute budget in Anchor, and that ticket records the measurement.
- The release profile sets `overflow-checks = true`, `lto = "fat"` and `codegen-units = 1`.
- On-chain code uses checked arithmetic and returns errors: no `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!` or unchecked indexing.
- Each program is built by its own manifest, never as a whole workspace, because a workspace build unifies dependency features and changes a program's bytes.

### Starting point

- Each strategy starts from Pipeline's Apache-2.0 strategy template (`templates/strategy`, generated with `scripts/new-strategy.sh` from a scratchpad clone), copied into this repo and owned here; the PR that adds it notes the Pipeline commit.
- The containment hook, which is a transfer-hook program and not a strategy, starts from Pipeline's Apache-2.0 `test-hook` allowlist hook (`programs/test-hook`).
- Pipeline's crates (`pipeline-strategy-interface`, `pipeline-client`, `pipeline-check`) are git dependencies pinned by `rev`, never by `branch` as the template ships them.
- The router's source (BSL 1.1 until 2028-11-08) is never copied in.

### Strategy rules

- Our strategies refuse bypass: `pipeline_swap` accepts only the router's market signer for that market, so every swap of ours goes through the router, pays the Pipeline fee and emits a swap event (ADR 0001).
- `pipeline_quote` and `pipeline_swap` call one shared pricing function (the template's `pricing.rs`), so a quote is exactly what the swap does.

### Test layers

Tests run against the real router.
A fixture script, from the template's `scripts/fetch-router.sh`, copies the router deployed on devnet into a gitignored fixtures folder and checks its hash against the hash pinned in the repo.
When MetalLegBob upgrades the devnet router the check fails, and a PR re-pins it deliberately after the tests pass against the new bytes.

1. **LiteSVM integration tests** of every instruction, through the router wherever the router is involved, with hostile cases modelled on Pipeline's `adversarial.rs` and `test-strategy-evil`: a wrong or missing market signer, bypass attempts, aliased and substituted accounts, and Token-2022 mints with a transfer fee and with a transfer hook.
2. **Maths proofs.** The maths lives in pure functions that take no accounts.
   Proptest runs at least 10,000 cases per property, and Kani proves them, with bounded harnesses by default and full-domain ones behind `--cfg kani_full` as in Pipeline.
   Z3 proves division and rounding where Kani cannot relate a division's output to its inputs.
   Book of Knowledge (see "Internal adversarial review") chooses the properties.
3. **Stateful invariant fuzzing**: Proptest generates sequences of swaps, custom actions and clock jumps against LiteSVM and checks after every step that value is conserved (no token is created or lost beyond the stated fees), that every holder can still exit, and that each quote equals its swap; each product's spec file adds its own invariants.
   Trident is not used: its stable release (0.12) is built on solana-sdk 2.3 and 0.13 has been a release candidate since 2026-05, so it cannot load Anchor 1.2 and Solana 3 and 4 crates.
   [Prior art for behavioural testing of Solana programs](/8/) found no fuzzer that fits better: Trident runs hand-written flows on its own SVM rather than LiteSVM.
   Revisit this if Trident moves to current Solana crates.
4. **Conformance**: every strategy's LiteSVM tests run `pipeline-check`'s `check_market` on their markets and require zero Fail and zero Warn.
5. **Limits**: a compute ceiling asserted per instruction, with headroom, and a call-depth test with hooked mints wherever a program calls another program inside a swap.
6. **Outside protocols**: wherever a program calls one (the lending AMM's lending market), its tests also run in LiteSVM loaded with that protocol's programs and accounts dumped from mainnet by a fixture script pinned to a slot, and against the protocol's devnet deployment if it has one.
7. **Devnet demo**: a script deploys the program, registers it, creates a market and swaps through the router with the TypeScript SDK, and every demo market passes `pipeline-check --url devnet --market <market> --fail-on-warn`.
8. **Canary checks**: once Aviary's Canary checks exist, our strategies must pass them on devnet, like any other strategy.

A `pipeline-check` Warn, in layer 4 or 7, is accepted only with a written reason in the program's spec file; a Skip for a feature the program refuses by design (such as exact-out) needs no reason.

### CI

- One GitHub Actions workflow, required to pass before any merge that touches on-chain code.
- It runs: a check that no keypair is in the repo (as Pipeline's `scripts/check-no-keypairs.sh`), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, each program's SBF build, test layers 1 to 5 (and 6 once its fixtures exist), and the Kani proofs and any Z3 proofs.
- The first on-chain build ticket adds it; that is the tax AMM's, the first product to build.
- Standard GitHub-hosted runners cost nothing on a public repository.

### Internal adversarial review

- Tools: Stronghold of Security (an adversarial audit) and Book of Knowledge (maths verification) from MetalLegBob's MIT-licensed Solana Vibes Kit (`https://github.com/MetalLegBob/solana-vibes-kit`), the process Pipeline's router went through twice.
  They are installed in this repo's `.claude/skills` at a pinned commit, by the first on-chain build ticket.
- Each program's last build ticket is its **hardening ticket**, run in a fresh session after its feature tickets have merged:
  - Round 1: a full Stronghold of Security audit and a Book of Knowledge pass; every confirmed finding gets a fix and a LiteSVM regression test named `sos_<finding id>`, as in Pipeline.
  - Round 2: Stronghold's verify phase and a re-audit of the code the fixes changed.
- The hardening ticket is done when no Critical, High or Medium finding is open; a Low finding is accepted only with the owner's written sign-off, recorded in the report.
- Reports go in `docs/security/<program>/`.
- Separately, every build PR gets `/code-review` at high effort before it merges.
- These reviews are internal and are never presented as audits, in metadata or anywhere else.

### Verified builds

- Every devnet deploy is a `solana-verify` (0.5.2 or later) Docker build with the same pins as Pipeline: `[workspace.metadata.cli] solana` chooses the Docker image (4.3.0 at `5ad130d`), `[workspace.metadata.solana] tools-version` chooses the platform tools, and the build passes `--arch v3`.
- Each deploy is recorded in `deployments/devnet.json`: program id, executable hash, commit and Docker image digest.
- After each deploy, `solana-verify get-program-hash -u devnet <program id>` must equal the build's executable hash; OtterSec's verified builds cover mainnet only, so on devnet we compare the hashes ourselves.
- Every program embeds a `security.txt` (the `solana-security-txt` crate) with the contact and the source repository.

### Published source

- The source is published from this repo, which must be public before the first devnet deploy of an on-chain program; making it public is the owner's action.
- `solana-verify verify-from-repo` takes this repo with the on-chain workspace as its mount path.
- The on-chain workspace carries its own Apache-2.0 `LICENSE` (ADR 0002).

### Metadata, IDL and conformance report

- Every strategy publishes complete `pipeline-strategy-metadata/1` metadata that passes `pipeline-client`'s validator with zero warnings.
- `source` names this repo, the deployed commit and the program's directory; `links.idl` points at the program's Anchor IDL; `conformance` points at the devnet demo's `pipeline-check` JSON report with its SHA-256; `security.contact` is set; and every `init` form and custom action is listed.
- The metadata, the IDL and the report are committed beside the program and linked through `raw.githubusercontent.com` at the commit hash, so the content behind a link never changes.
- Each deploy updates the router's metadata URI for the strategy.
- `security.audits` stays empty.

### Upgrade authority

- On devnet every program stays upgradeable, under one project upgrade-authority key, `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/upgrade-authority.json`, separate from the wallet that pays for deploys (`wallet.json`) and never committed.
  The upgrade authority also signs `register_strategy` and pays its listing fee, so it holds a little devnet SOL.
- Nothing is frozen on devnet while Pipeline's interfaces can still change.
- Aviary gives our programs no exemption and no trusted badge: Canary checks and trust facts show them as upgradeable by a single key, exactly as they would anyone else's.
- Each product's spec file states the product's intended mainnet upgrade policy: a multisig with a timelock, then frozen once stable, unless the product says otherwise.
  The containment hook is the most sensitive, because an upgrade to it could block every contained token's transfers.
  Carrying the policy out belongs to the mainnet launch effort.

### What each product's spec file adds

- Its intended mainnet upgrade policy.
- Its compute ceilings per instruction.
- Its invariants for test layer 3, beyond the shared three.
- Any accepted `pipeline-check` Warn, with the reason.
- What its Aviary panel shows and which actions its metadata exposes.

documents.title: Containment hook
documents.body:
## What it is

- One Token-2022 transfer hook program, deployed once, that serves every contained token.
- While a token is contained, every transfer of it must go into or come out of its one home market; everything else is refused.
- Once its home market has collected the unlock goal in tax, or its unlock deadline passes, anyone can unlock it: the hook removes itself and the token becomes an ordinary Token-2022 token, tradable everywhere.
- In v1 every home market is a tax AMM market whose tax side is the quote mint, on devnet only.

## Lifecycle

1. The launcher creates the mint with the transfer hook pointing at this program and the token's unlock PDA as hook authority, and mints the supply (minting never calls the hook).
2. The launcher creates the home market on the tax AMM, binds it and seeds it (see "Launch in v1").
3. While contained, the token trades only in its home market, and its tax builds up there.
4. Once the unlock is due, anyone calls `unlock`.
5. After the unlock, Token-2022 no longer calls any hook for this mint.

Until `bind`, the hook refuses every transfer, so no liquidity can go in before the rules are fixed.

## Accounts

All are PDAs of the containment hook program, one set per contained mint.

| Account | Seeds | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Config | `["config", mint]` | The mint, the home market (the router's `Market` address), its market state, the token's vault in it, its fee account, the quote mint, the unlock goal, the unlock deadline, when it was bound, when it was unlocked (or never), bumps |
| Validation account | `["extra-account-metas", mint]` (the standard transfer hook interface seed) | One extra account for Token-2022 to pass on every transfer: the config, read-only |
| Unlock PDA | `["unlock", mint]` | No data; it is the mint's transfer hook authority and signs the unlock |

The config is never closed, so it stays as the record of the token's containment after the unlock.

## Binding (`bind`)

- Signed by the mint's mint authority, which is how the hook knows the caller is the launcher; nobody else can bind a mint, so binding cannot be front-run.
- Creates the config and the validation account; it fails if the config already exists, which makes binding write-once.
- No instruction changes the config afterwards: not the launcher, not us.
- Arguments: the unlock goal (greater than zero, in quote-mint base units) and the unlock deadline (a Unix timestamp later than now and at most 90 days after the binding).

### Checks on the mint

- Owned by Token-2022.
- Its transfer hook program is this program, and its transfer hook authority is its unlock PDA.
- Its only extensions are on an allowlist: transfer hook, metadata pointer, token metadata, group pointer, group member pointer, token group and token group member (the tax AMM's own mint allowlist, none of which gives power over anyone's balance).
  Every other extension is refused, including permanent delegate (it can move or burn anyone's tokens), confidential transfer (the hook would see `u64::MAX` instead of the amount), default account state (accounts that start frozen), transfer fee (Token-2022 withdraws withheld fees without calling the hook, an escape route), pausable, and any extension Token-2022 adds later.
- Its freeze authority is unset, because freezing the home market's vault would trap every holder with nowhere else to sell; this is stricter than the tax AMM, which allows freeze authorities.
- The mint authority may stay set; the launcher can revoke it after binding, and Canary checks report it as they do for any mint.

### Checks on the home market

- The `Market` account is owned by Pipeline's router and sits at its PDA `["market", strategy, market_state]`.
- Its strategy is the tax AMM, whose program id is fixed in the hook at build time.
- One of its two mints is the contained mint; the other is the quote mint.
- The market state passed in is the one the `Market` records, owned by the tax AMM, and its tax side is the quote mint's index, so its tax collected is counted in the quote mint.
- `bind` reads the token's vault from `Market.vaults` and derives the fee account (the Token-2022 associated token account of the router PDA `["fees", market]` for the contained mint), rather than taking either from the caller.

One home market per token: several would split the liquidity that containment exists to concentrate, and summing tax in different quote mints would need a price on chain.

## The allow rule

The hook's `Execute` fails closed: it refuses the transfer unless all of these hold.

- The validation account and the config are present and at their PDAs for this mint, and the mint is the one Token-2022 is transferring.
- The source token account has Token-2022's `transferring` flag set, so nobody can call `Execute` directly.
- The source or the destination is one of the two allowed accounts: the home market's vault for the token, or the market's fee account for the token.

It makes no CPI, because on a buy it already runs at the last call level the runtime allows (router, strategy, Token-2022, hook).
The allowed sets are the same for sources and destinations, and neither allowed account is controlled by a wallet: the vault is moved only by the tax AMM and the fee account only by the router's `sweep_fees`.

### What this allows

- Buys and sells through the router (sells pass on the destination, buys on the source).
- The Pipeline fee on sells, paid in the token into the fee account.
- `sweep_fees`, which moves the fee account to Pipeline's treasury (it passes on the source, so the treasury needs no entry).
- The tax AMM's one-time `seed` into the vault.
- The tax AMM's `distribute`, which pays tax out of the vault; with the tax side on the quote mint it never moves the contained token anyway.

Bypass needs no rule: the tax AMM refuses it, so every trade in the home market goes through the router, pays Pipeline's fee and counts in the market's counters.

### What this refuses

- Every wallet-to-wallet transfer, including between a holder's own wallets and to a CEX deposit address; a holder who wants to move the token sells it and buys again.
- Funding a second market for the token anywhere, on Pipeline or elsewhere, and paying out of one.
- Any integrator fee on a sell, because the router pays it in the token into the integrator's own account, which is not allowed.
  Integrators must pass a zero integrator fee on sells of a contained token (at zero the router makes no transfer); buys pay their integrator fee in the quote mint as usual.

A buy may deliver the token to anyone's account, since the router does not check who owns the output account; that account can then only sell into the home market, so it is a gift, not an escape.

## Unlock (`unlock`)

- Permissionless: any signer can call it and pays the transaction fee.
- Due when either holds:
  - the home market's `tax_collected`, read from the tax AMM market state recorded at binding (owner and address checked), is at least the unlock goal;
  - the clock's Unix timestamp is at or past the unlock deadline.
- Signed by the unlock PDA, it calls Token-2022's `TransferHookInstruction::Update` with no program id, then `SetAuthority(TransferHookProgramId, None)`, and records the unlock time in the config.
- Both fields must be cleared: Meteora's DAMM v2 and DLMM accept a mint with the transfer hook extension permissionlessly only when the hook program and the hook authority are both unset.
- A second call fails, because the authority is gone.

There is no keeper job for the unlock in v1.
Nothing breaks while an unlock waits, since sells into the home market keep working, and whoever wants out or wants the token trading elsewhere can press Aviary's Unlock button.

### After the unlock

- Token-2022 skips the hook; the mint keeps a transfer hook extension with both fields unset, as graduated Meteora DBC mints do.
- Integrators stop passing hook accounts; stale ones are ignored.
- The deprecated `Transfer` instruction without a mint still fails for this mint, as for any mint with the extension; wallets and routers use `transfer_checked`.

## Unlock goal

- The tax collected by the home market, in quote-mint base units (lamports when the quote mint is wrapped SOL): the tax AMM's `tax_collected` counter, which only router swaps change, buys and sells alike.
- Why the tax AMM counts it and not the hook: ADR 0006.
- Set by the launcher at binding and never changed.
- Why tax collected rather than volume:
  - A tax authority may lower its market's taxes to the bottom of a range fixed at creation, which may be 0, and the tax AMM has no LP fee; at a 0% tax, faking volume would cost only Pipeline's 0.25%, so a vamp could wait for a low-tax window and force a permanent unlock cheaply.
  - Counting tax collected, forcing an early unlock always costs a third party the whole goal in tax, whatever the rate; at 0% the goal stops moving and the deadline unlocks the token.
  - It measures what containment protects: the token's tax income, until it has earned a set amount.
- The only party who can reach the goal cheaply is whoever receives the tax (they pay Pipeline's fee and the suite share and get the rest back), and they would be undoing their own protection.
- No minimum age: the deadline already bounds how long containment lasts, and the goal is the launcher's commitment.

## Unlock deadline

- Required at binding, at most 90 days after it; once it passes, the unlock is due even if the goal was never met.
- A contained token is a honeypot by construction if its home market stops working, for example after a bad tax AMM upgrade or a router upgrade that changes the fee account's derivation; the deadline caps how long holders can be stuck.

## Hook accounts callers must pass

- Every transfer of a contained token needs the same tail: the hook program, the validation account and the config, read-only.
- Sells put it in the router's `input_hook_accounts`; buys put it after the strategy's own accounts; `sweep_fees` takes it as remaining accounts; the tax AMM's `seed` takes it after its own accounts.
- Neither Pipeline client resolves hook accounts, and Pipeline's hosted API refuses to build swaps whose input mint has a transfer hook (`docs/API.md` at `5ad130d`), so Aviary, our scripts and anyone sweeping fees resolve them from the validation account and build those transactions with the SDK; a call that leaves them out is refused.

## Launch in v1

- A devnet CLI script in this repo launches a contained token.
  - Create the mint with only allowed extensions and no freeze authority, with the hook and its authority set as in "Lifecycle", and mint the supply.
  - Then the tax AMM's market creation (`docs/spec/tax-amm.md`, "Creating a market") with `bind` inserted before the seed: the router's `create_market` with the tax side on the quote mint, `init_fee_account` for each mint, `bind` with the goal and deadline given as required flags (no defaults), then the tax AMM's `seed`.
- `bind` belongs in the same transaction as the market's creation, but may go in a later one with the seed if the transaction is too large: nothing can move the token before `bind`, the market is closed to swaps until its seed, and only the seeder can seed.
- Revoking the mint authority is an optional last step; it must come after `bind`, which needs the mint authority's signature, or the token can never be bound and never transfer.
- Graduating a contained token from a launchpad through `pipeline_seed_liquidity` is not supported in v1, because the seed would move tokens before the `Market` account that `bind` reads exists.
- Aviary v1 does not launch new tokens (`docs/spec/pipescope.md`), so the script is the only way to launch a contained token.
  The tax AMM's launch form in Aviary refuses a mint whose transfer hook is ours, since its seed would fail for a token not yet bound and a bound token already has its home market.

## In Aviary

`docs/spec/pipescope.md` has each product add its own panel to Aviary; this is the containment hook's, built with its build tickets.
The hook is not a strategy and has no strategy metadata, so its panel and its one action are built into Aviary rather than rendered from metadata.

- **Recognising a contained token**: its transfer hook program is ours, its hook authority is its unlock PDA, and its config exists.
- **Panel**, on the home market's page:
  - "Contained": the token can only be bought and sold in this market until it unlocks, and cannot be sent to another wallet;
  - the tax collected against the unlock goal, in the quote mint, as a number and a bar;
  - the unlock deadline, as a date and the time left;
  - once unlocked: when, and whether by the goal or the deadline.
- **Unlock button**: shown to anyone once the unlock is due; it sends `unlock` from the connected wallet.
- **Trade box**: before a buy of a contained token, the same one-line rule as the panel.
- **Swaps**: Aviary resolves the hook accounts for every swap of a hooked token, ours included, and builds those swaps with the SDK, since Pipeline's hosted API refuses them.
- **Integrator fee**: nothing to add; Aviary charges its fee only when the trader pays in SOL or USDC, so sells of a contained token already carry none.
- The facts panel shows the mint's `transfer-hook` and `transfer-hook-authority` trust flags until the unlock clears them, so traders who hide hooked tokens by those flags also hide contained ones.

## Depends on

- The tax AMM (`docs/spec/tax-amm.md`): `tax_collected` and the tax side at fixed offsets that later versions never move, vaults at PDAs `["vault", market_state, mint]`, bypass refused, liquidity locked, tax paid out of the vault only, and the program frozen before mainnet because the unlock trusts its counter.
- `docs/spec/README.md`, the engineering and security bar every program of ours meets; "Building it" below adds what it asks of each product's file.
- Pipeline's router: the fee account's derivation belongs to the router, which is upgradeable on devnet; if an upgrade changed it, sells of contained tokens would fail until their deadline.

## Ruled out

- Allowing wallet-to-wallet transfers between keypair wallets signed by their owner: it needs an on-curve check, and an RFQ market maker quoting from a hot wallet could still take the home market's trading.
- A launcher-set list of integrator fee accounts allowed as destinations: it makes the allow rule asymmetric and gives launchers a list that could name a bid-only vamp pool, for a fee that only lasts until the unlock.
- Volume as the unlock goal, with or without a minimum-tax floor checked at binding: without a floor it is cheap to fake in a low-tax window, and a floor needs an arbitrary constant while still letting a third party force the unlock for the floor times the goal.
- Counting the goal in the hook, which would also count liquidity moves and donations, or from transfers into the fee account, which donations could fake; or a wrapper program reading the router's return data, which misses direct router swaps.
- A tax side on the contained token for home markets: the goal would be counted in the token itself, whose price the launcher's supply sets.
- Several home markets per token.
- Changing the goal or the deadline after binding, even only lowering them.
- A minimum age as part of the goal.
- A keeper job for the unlock in v1.
- Launchpad graduation into a contained home market in v1.
- Keeping `test-hook`'s fail-open path (see "Starting point").
- An upgradeable hook on mainnet, even under a multisig with a timelock.

## Building it

What `docs/spec/README.md` asks each product's spec file to add, and how this program meets the bar.

### Starting point

- The bar starts the hook from Pipeline's Apache-2.0 `test-hook` (`programs/test-hook`), for its licence and its extra-account-meta setup.
- `test-hook` approves every transfer when its whitelist account is left out (still so at `5ad130d`), and Token-2022 calls a hook without its extra accounts whenever a caller leaves them out, so that path is replaced by the fail-closed rule in "The allow rule"; the research's citations of the Factory's transfer hook show the checks to add (the `transferring` flag, the mint's owner, the validation account's seeds), read as a pattern, not copied.
- Pipeline crates are pinned to `rev = "5ad130d"`, as for the tax AMM; build and test with the toolchain in `docs/toolchain.md`.

### Upgrade policy

- On devnet the hook stays upgradeable under the project upgrade-authority key, as the bar says.
- It is frozen (upgrade authority removed) before any mainnet use, rather than the bar's default of a multisig with a timelock: the hook's whole promise is that nobody can change the rules, and a key that can upgrade it could block every contained token's transfers at once.
- The cost is that a bug found after freezing cannot be fixed; the mainnet launch effort, out of scope here, audits the hook before freezing it.

### Compute ceilings

Tests assert the measured cost of each instruction with headroom, never above these ceilings.

| Instruction | Ceiling (CU) | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Execute` | 10,000 | Runs on two transfers in every sell and one in every buy, inside the trader's swap; it uses bumps stored in the config instead of searching for them |
| `bind` | 60,000 | Creates two accounts and reads the mint's extensions, the router's `Market` and the market state |
| `unlock` | 30,000 | Two Token-2022 calls signed by the unlock PDA |

### Invariants

For the bar's stateful fuzzing layer, beyond its shared three:

1. While contained, no sequence of actions moves the token between two accounts that are both outside the home vault and the fee account.
2. A transfer that leaves out or substitutes any hook account is refused.
3. The config never changes after binding, except the unlock time, which is set once.
4. `unlock` succeeds exactly when the tax collected reaches the goal or the deadline has passed; afterwards both of the mint's hook fields are unset, and nothing else ever changes them.
5. The shared "every holder can still exit" invariant holds for contained tokens, through sells into the home market.

### Not applicable

- `pipeline-check` Warns and strategy metadata: the hook is not a strategy; its Aviary panel and action are in "In Aviary".

### Done means

- LiteSVM tests through the real router with a tax AMM home market cover: buys, sells, the Pipeline fee and `sweep_fees` with the hook tail; refusal of wallet-to-wallet transfers, of a second market's funding, of a sell with a non-zero integrator fee and of every transfer missing a hook account or calling `Execute` directly; `bind`'s refusal of each refused extension, of a freeze authority, of a wrong signer, of a market on another strategy, of a tax side on the contained token, of a deadline beyond 90 days and of a second `bind`; `unlock` by the goal, by the deadline, its refusal before either, and a second `unlock`; and transfers skipping the hook afterwards.
- The invariants above under the fuzzing layer, and the compute ceilings and a call-depth test on buys under the limits layer.
- On devnet: the hook deployed; a contained token launched by the script, bought and sold through the router with the SDK, a wallet-to-wallet transfer refused, then unlocked by a short deadline, with the mint showing both hook fields unset.
- Whatever else `docs/spec/README.md` requires of our on-chain programs.

## Not measured yet

- The compute cost of the hook on each hooked transfer: into the vault and into the fee account on a sell, out of the vault on a buy; measured in the build against the ceilings above.
- Whether the creation transaction with `bind` fits in one transaction with an address lookup table; if not, `bind` and the seed go in a second one, as above.

documents.title: Lending AMM
documents.body:
## What it is

- A Pipeline strategy whose markets are two-mint constant-product pools with open LP shares.
- One mint of each market is the lent side, WSOL or USDC; most of the lent side is lent to Kamino Lend through its cToken instructions, and a buffer stays in the market's own vault for swaps.
- Prices come from the market's total reserves: the other side's vault, and on the lent side the buffer plus the market's cTokens valued at Kamino's exchange rate.
- A swap that must pay out more of the lent side than the buffer holds redeems just the shortfall from Kamino in the same swap; a swap never deposits into Kamino.
- A permissionless keeper job, `rebalance`, moves the buffer back to its target when it drifts out of its band.
- The LP fee and all the lending yield go to LPs, through the value of their shares.
- The program has no admin: nobody, us included, can pause it, change a market or move a market to another reserve; it reacts to Kamino's own state.

## Not in v1

- Exact-out swaps.
- Lending both sides of a market, or any lent mint other than WSOL and USDC.
- Any lending market other than Kamino Lend: Jupiter Lend is out of scope for this map (see the map's Out of scope), and so are Kamino's obligations, which refuse calls from our program (`CpiDisabled`).
- Kamino withdrawal tickets: issuance is switched off on Kamino's main market (2026-11-09), so the program never enqueues one.
- A buffer target or band chosen per market.
- A share of the yield or the LP fee for us or for the market's creator.
- Markets with more than two mints.
- On-chain token metadata for LP mints.
- Mainnet: nothing deploys there before Pipeline's router does, and the program is frozen first (see "Upgrades and freezing").

## Constants

| Name | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BUFFER_TARGET_BPS` | 2000 (20%) | The buffer's target share of the lent side's total |
| `BUFFER_MIN_BPS`, `BUFFER_MAX_BPS` | 1000, 3000 | The band; `rebalance` acts only when the buffer's share is outside it |
| `MIN_REBALANCE` | 0.05 SOL (50,000,000 lamports) for WSOL, 5 USDC (5,000,000 base units) for USDC | Smaller moves are skipped |
| `WITHDRAW_MODE_ENTER` | 5 | Enter withdraw mode when Kamino's freely available liquidity is below 5 times the market's lent value |
| `WITHDRAW_MODE_EXIT` | 10 | Leave withdraw mode when it is back above 10 times |
| `MAX_LP_FEE_BPS` | 200 (2%) | The highest LP fee a market may charge |
| `MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY` | 1,000 LP base units | Locked for good by the first deposit |
| `LP_DECIMALS` | 9 | Decimals of every market's LP mint |
| `KLEND_PROGRAM` | `KLend2g3cP87fffoy8q1mQqGKjrxjC8boSyAYavgmjD` | Kamino Lend, the same id on devnet and mainnet |
| `LENT_MINTS` | per cluster, below | The lent mints and the one Kamino reserve each lends to |

`LENT_MINTS`, selected at build time by a cluster feature (`devnet` or `mainnet`):

| Cluster | Lent mint | Lending market | Reserve |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mainnet | WSOL `So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112` | Kamino main market `7u3HeHxYDLhnCoErrtycNokbQYbWGzLs6JSDqGAv5PfF` | SOL `d4A2prbA2whesmvHaL88BH6Ewn5N4bTSU2Ze8P6Bc4Q` |
| mainnet | USDC `EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v` | Kamino main market | USDC `D6q6wuQSrifJKZYpR1M8R4YawnLDtDsMmWM1NbBmgJ59` |
| devnet | WSOL | Our own Kamino lending market (see "Devnet") | Our WSOL reserve |
| devnet | Our test USDC mint, 6 decimals | Our own Kamino lending market | Our test USDC reserve |

- Market creators never choose a reserve: a reserve in a lending market the creator owned could be reconfigured to let its owner borrow the LPs' deposits away.
- The devnet addresses are filled in by the build ticket that creates our devnet lending market.
- The constants are compiled into the program; changing one is a program upgrade, which ends when the program is frozen.

## Markets

### Shape

- Exactly two mints: the lent mint, which must be on the cluster's `LENT_MINTS` list, and the other mint.
- The mints must differ.
- If both mints are on the list (a SOL and USDC market), the creator's `lent_index` decides which one is lent, and the other is never lent.
  Such a market is allowed but pointless next to cheaper SOL and USDC venues, since every hop pays Pipeline's 0.25%.
- `pipeline_market_info` reports the mints in the order the creator gave them, with `supports_exact_out = false`.

### Mint rules

- The lent side is exactly the listed mint, owned by SPL Token.
- The other side follows the tax AMM's mint rules (`tax-amm.md`, "Mint rules"): SPL Token, or Token-2022 with only transfer hook, metadata pointer, token metadata, group pointer, group member pointer, token group and token group member extensions; transfer fees, permanent delegates and every other extension are refused at creation.
- So hooked tokens may trade in a lending AMM market.
  The hooked transfer and the Kamino redeem are sibling calls under the strategy and never stack: the deepest chain is the redeem, router (1), strategy (2), klend (3), SPL Token (4), or 5 when the trader uses a smart wallet, inside the limit of 5.
  A transfer hook that makes calls of its own fails for smart-wallet traders, as it does in any Pipeline market.
- A contained token can only trade in its home market until its unlock, and Kamino refuses hooked mints, so a contained token is never lent.

### Addresses

- The market state is the PDA `["market", other_mint, lent_mint, lp_fee_bps as u16 little-endian]` of the lending AMM program, so there is one market per pair, lent side and fee.
  Every creation parameter is in the seeds, so nobody can occupy a market's address with other parameters.
  Someone may create a market first at a bad price with dust liquidity; correcting that price by a swap costs little, and the locked minimum stops share inflation.
- Markets created through `pipeline_seed_liquidity` live at `["seeded", seeder, other_mint, lent_mint, lp_fee_bps]` instead, as Pipeline's guide asks, so nobody can create or price them first.
- The vault authority is the PDA `["authority", market_state]`, a data-less address that signs every transfer out of the vaults, owns the cToken account, signs Kamino calls as the depositor and is the LP mint's mint authority.
- Each vault is a token account at `["vault", market_state, mint]`, owned by the vault authority; the lent mint's vault holds the buffer.
- The cToken account is a token account at `["ctoken", market_state]` for the reserve's collateral mint, owned by the vault authority; each market holds its own cTokens.
- The LP mint is an SPL Token mint at `["lp_mint", market_state]`, with `LP_DECIMALS` decimals, the vault authority as mint authority and no freeze authority.
- The lock account is the vault authority's associated token account for the LP mint; no instruction ever moves LP shares out of it.
- Metadata describes all of them as `pda:` sources, so the SDK can resolve them before the market exists.

### Creation parameters

`init_data` is the Borsh encoding of:

| Field | Type | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lent_index` | u8 | 0 or 1: which of the two mints is lent; it must be on the cluster's `LENT_MINTS` list |
| `lp_fee_bps` | u16 | At most `MAX_LP_FEE_BPS`; Aviary's form defaults it to 30 (0.30%) |

- `pipeline_init_market` refuses anything that breaks a rule, checks that the market state's address is the PDA above, checks that the market signer is the router's PDA `["market", program, market_state]` and stores it, creates the vaults, the cToken account and the LP mint idempotently, and records the reserve, the creation slot and the Unix time.
- Rent comes from the router's payer, funded by the creator's `max_creator_lamports`.

### Creating a market

One transaction, as Pipeline's guide recommends:

1. The router's `create_market` with the creation parameters.
2. The router's `init_fee_account` for each of the two mints.
3. The lending AMM's `add_liquidity`, which makes the first deposit.

Until the first deposit, quotes and swaps are refused, because an empty side cannot be priced.

## Valuing the lent side

### Total reserves

- The other side's reserve `R` is what the market has recorded in its vault.
- The lent side's reserve is `L = B + V`, where `B` is the buffer the market has recorded in its lent-mint vault and `V` is the value of the cTokens it has recorded, `V = floor(c x S_total / S_ctoken)`.
- `S_total` is the reserve's total supply, `total_available_amount + borrowed_amount_sf - accumulated_protocol_fees_sf - accumulated_referrer_fees_sf - pending_referrer_fees_sf` (fixed point with 60 fractional bits where the field ends in `_sf`), and `S_ctoken` is the reserve's own `collateral.mint_total_supply`, never the SPL mint's supply, which differs by the 100,000-unit seed on new reserves and by 13.8M on mainnet USDC.
- Field offsets are in the Kamino facts, section 4, at klend 1.28.0.
- Tokens or cTokens sent to the market outside its own instructions are donations: never credited, never priced and never paid out.

### The stored rate, everywhere

- Quotes, swaps, adding liquidity and `rebalance` all value cTokens at the rate stored in the reserve account, with no projection to the current slot.
- The stored rate lagged 2 to 68 seconds behind on 2026-11-09, which understates the value by about 0.05 bps an hour of lag, far below any fee; it is always an understatement, because interest only raises the rate.
- Projecting it would mean copying Kamino's interest maths into our program, where any drift from Kamino's own would misprice.

### Kamino's losses fall on LPs

- The rate can fall: Kamino's lending market owner can write off bad debt with `socialize_loss`, which lowers the reserve's total supply.
- A market's lent value, and so its price and every LP share, falls with it pro rata; there is no insurance fund.
- Bad debt Kamino has not yet written off still counts as borrowed, so until then the stored rate overstates what the cTokens can fetch.
- If a write-off reaches the reserve's whole supply, Kamino deprecates the reserve and redeems stop for good; the market then behaves as under emergency mode (see "When Kamino can't pay").

### Checking the reserve before reading it

- Every instruction that reads the reserve first checks its address (the constant for the lent mint), owner (`KLEND_PROGRAM`), size (8624 bytes), Anchor account discriminator, lending market, liquidity mint and collateral mint.
- On any mismatch, such as a Kamino upgrade that changes the layout, it refuses rather than misprices: quotes, swaps, adding liquidity and `rebalance` fail.
- Removing liquidity in kind never reads the reserve, so a Kamino change can stop trading but can never trap LPs.

## Swaps

### Pricing

Exact-in only, so `pipeline_market_info` reports `supports_exact_out = false` and an exact-out quote or swap is refused.

For a trade from side `i` to side `o`, with effective reserves `E` (`R` for the other side, `L` for the lent side) and credited input `a`:

- `a_net = a - ceil(a x lp_fee_bps / 10,000)` and `out = floor(E_o x a_net / (E_i + a_net))`.
- The whole of `a` joins side `i`, so the LP fee stays in the market and accrues to LPs.
- Intermediate maths is in u128; the fee rounds up and the output rounds down, so the product of the effective reserves never falls.
- Input is credited with Pipeline's `credited_input`: what the input vault holds beyond what the market has recorded there, capped at what the router sent.
- The input stays in the input vault for the whole swap, as Pipeline's guide asks; lent-side input simply joins the buffer.
- A quote or swap is refused when `out` is 0, when the other side would pay out its whole reserve, or when the lent side would pay out more than the buffer plus what Kamino can pay right now.

### Redeeming the shortfall

- When the output is the lent side and `out` exceeds the buffer `B`, the swap redeems the shortfall `s = out - B` from Kamino before paying the trader.
- It burns `ceil(s x S_ctoken / S_total)` cTokens with `redeem_reserve_collateral`; Kamino refreshes the reserve inside that call, so the rate it pays at is at least the stored rate, and the market receives at least `s`.
- The market measures what actually arrived in its vault; anything above `s` stays in the buffer.
- What Kamino can pay right now is the smallest of: the reserve's freely available liquidity (`total_available_amount` minus the value of queued withdrawal tickets), what remains of its withdrawal cap in the current interval, and the value of the market's own cTokens; it is zero while either emergency mode is on or the reserve is deprecated.
- `pipeline_quote` and `pipeline_swap` call the same pricing function on the same reserve fields, so a quote shows whether a trade redeems and refuses a trade Kamino could not pay, and `pipeline-check`'s `quote_matches_swap` verifies quotes on both sides of the buffer's edge.

### Accounts

- `pipeline_resolve_accounts` receives the trade, so it lists the Kamino redeem accounts (klend, lending market, lending market authority, reserve liquidity supply, reserve collateral mint, both token programs, the instructions sysvar) and marks the reserve writable only when the trade's quote needs a redeem.
- Ordinary swaps then pass the reserve read-only, for valuation, and never write-lock Kamino's reserve, which every Kamino user of that mint shares.
- A swap that needs a redeem but was built without those accounts, because the buffer shrank between quote and swap, fails cleanly with its own error, and the integrator resolves again.
- A swap that redeems costs about 30k compute units more (Kamino's redeem, mainnet median 29,670).

### Bypass

- Refused: `pipeline_swap` accepts only the router's market signer stored at creation, as in the tax AMM.
- So every trade pays Pipeline's fee and emits a swap event.
- No custom action moves the price.

## The buffer and `rebalance`

### The rule

- The buffer's share is `B / L`.
- Inside the band (`BUFFER_MIN_BPS` to `BUFFER_MAX_BPS`), `rebalance` does nothing and fails with `WithinBand`, so a keeper's simulation shows there is nothing to do and nobody pays for a no-op.
- Above the band it deposits `B - L x BUFFER_TARGET_BPS / 10,000` into Kamino with `deposit_reserve_liquidity`; below the band it redeems `L x BUFFER_TARGET_BPS / 10,000 - B`, capped at what Kamino can pay right now.
- A move smaller than `MIN_REBALANCE` is skipped.
- The market measures the cTokens or liquidity that actually moved and records them.
- The market state also keeps running totals of the liquidity it has deposited into Kamino and redeemed from it, in swaps and removals as well, so its lending yield so far is `V + redeemed - deposited`.
- With 20% held back, a sell that drops the price by about a third is paid from the buffer alone.

### Withdraw mode

- `rebalance` checks Kamino's freely available liquidity against the market's lent value `V`.
- Below `WITHDRAW_MODE_ENTER` times `V`, the market enters withdraw mode: `rebalance` redeems everything Kamino can pay and deposits nothing.
- Above `WITHDRAW_MODE_EXIT` times `V`, it leaves withdraw mode and the band applies again.
- On 2026-11-09 Kamino's SOL reserve had about 218,000 SOL free at 90.9% utilisation, and it blocks new borrowing above 90%, so withdraw mode only bites in a real crunch, and then our LPs leave early rather than last.

### When it runs

- `rebalance {}` is a permissionless custom action: anyone may call it at any time, and inside the band it does nothing, so it cannot be used to grief a market.
- It creates no accounts, so the caller pays only the transaction fee, and gets no tip.
- Our keeper runner calls it when Aviary's indexer sees a swap or an LP action leave a market outside its band, and sweeps every lending AMM market every 10 minutes for withdraw mode and anything missed.
- That is the lending AMM's whole answer for the map's keeper runner: one keeper job per market, triggered by events, a few calls an hour at most.
  Kamino's `withdraw_queued_liquidity` is not needed, since the program never holds a withdrawal ticket.

## When Kamino can't pay

The program has no switches of its own; it reads Kamino's state at each call.

| Kamino's state | Swaps | `rebalance` | Adding liquidity | Removing liquidity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Normal | Buffer, then redeem the shortfall | Band and withdraw mode as above | Allowed | Cash or in kind |
| Little free liquidity, or withdrawal cap used up | Up to the buffer plus what Kamino can pay | Redeems what it can; withdraw mode if below the threshold | Allowed | Cash if Kamino can pay the LP's share, else in kind |
| `block_ctoken_usage` set (only Kamino's global admin can) | As normal | Skips deposits, still redeems | Allowed | Cash or in kind |
| Reserve or market emergency mode | Buffer only | Refuses | Allowed | In kind |
| Reserve deprecated after a total write-off | Buffer only, for good | Refuses | Refused | In kind |
| Reserve fails the layout check | Refused | Refuses | Refused | In kind |

- Kamino has used reserve emergency mode on its main market once in the period checked: the ETH reserve's redeems were blocked for about 16 hours from 2026-04-23 19:58 UTC, during the Kelp exploit; SOL and USDC were never touched.
- Our own devnet lending market lets the demo turn emergency mode on and off for real.

## Liquidity and LP shares

### Shares

- A market's share count is `N = LP mint supply + MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY`; the locked minimum is never minted, so it can never be withdrawn.
- LP shares burned with SPL Token's burn leave the count, which hands their value to the remaining LPs; to keep liquidity in the market for good, send shares to the lock account instead (see `lock_lp`).

### Adding

`add_liquidity { max_other: u64, max_lent: u64, min_lp: u64 }`, signed by the LP:

- The first deposit takes both amounts in full, both above 0, sets the price, and mints `isqrt(other x lent) - MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY` shares; it fails if that is not above 0.
- Later deposits take both mints at the current ratio `R : L`, with the lent side valued at its total, mint `min(other x N / R, lent x N / L)` shares rounded down, and take only the amounts those shares are worth, rounded up.
- The lent-side deposit joins the buffer; `rebalance` lends it later, so adding never calls Kamino.
- It refuses if fewer than `min_lp` shares would be minted, and while the reserve is deprecated or fails the layout check.

### Removing

`remove_liquidity { lp: u64, min_other: u64, min_lent: u64, in_kind: bool }`, signed by the LP, who burns `lp` shares and receives pro rata, each part rounded down:

- the other side: `R x lp / N`, from its vault;
- the buffer's part: `B x lp / N`, in the lent mint;
- the cTokens' part: `c x lp / N` cTokens.

With `in_kind = false` the cTokens' part is redeemed from Kamino and paid in the lent mint, so the LP receives only the two mints; if Kamino cannot pay that part right now, the instruction fails before calling Kamino, and `min_lent` protects against a rate move.
With `in_kind = true` the cTokens' part is paid as cTokens into the LP's associated token account for the collateral mint, created at the LP's expense; this path reads no Kamino account and calls no Kamino instruction, so it works whatever state Kamino is in.
Aviary offers in kind whenever a cash removal would fail.
Either way the buffer's share of the market is unchanged, so one LP leaving never drains the buffer traders rely on.

### Seeding

- `pipeline_seed_liquidity` takes `SeedRequest.data` as the Borsh encoding of `{ lent_index: u8, lp_fee_bps: u16 }`, under the same rules as creation.
- It creates the market at the seeder-scoped address, takes at most `amounts[i]` from each escrow, opens the market at the price those amounts imply, mints the first deposit's shares to the associated token account of the LP recipient (seed account 4) for the LP mint, and returns `SeedResult { taken, lp_amount }`.
- A launchpad that wants the liquidity locked names the market's vault authority as the LP recipient, which puts the shares straight into the lock account.
- The caller then records the market with the router's `register_existing_market` and `init_fee_account` for each mint, in the same transaction.

## Who earns what

- LPs: the LP fee and all the lending yield, pro rata through their shares, and Kamino's losses likewise.
- Pipeline: its 0.25% router fee on every swap.
- Us: nothing from the strategy; Aviary earns its integrator fee on the trades it routes.
- A market's creator: nothing beyond their own LP shares.

## Custom actions and metadata

| Action | Metadata `kind` | Signer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `add_liquidity` | `add_liquidity` | The LP |
| `remove_liquidity` | `remove_liquidity` | The LP |
| `lock_lp` | `other` | The LP |
| `rebalance` | `other` | Anyone |

- Every action that moves the other mint forwards transfer-hook accounts after its own, as the template's swap does.
- Each instruction emits an event (market created, liquidity added, liquidity removed with the in-kind amount, shares locked, rebalanced with the amount and direction, withdraw mode entered or left, a swap's redeem with its amount) so Aviary's indexer can show a market's history; Aviary reads current values from the market state and the reserve, not from events.
- The metadata follows `pipeline-strategy-metadata/1` at `5ad130d`: name, description, category `amm`, tags including `lending` and `kamino`, links including `source` and the IDL, `init` as above with `market_state` as a `pda:` source, every action above, `security.contact`, and `conformance` pointing at a published `pipeline-check` report and its SHA-256.

## Aviary's panel

Aviary's lending AMM panel shows, per market:

- the lent side, its Kamino reserve and lending market, with links;
- the buffer, the lent value and the buffer's share against its band, and whether the market is in withdraw mode;
- the largest sell the buffer pays alone, and the largest Kamino can pay right now on top;
- Kamino's utilisation, freely available liquidity, supply rate, emergency modes and `block_ctoken_usage` for the reserve;
- the LP fee, LP share value, locked shares, and the market's lending yield so far;
- the actions above as forms, with in kind offered whenever a cash removal would fail.

The explainer's fact table carries the same facts, and its risks for every lending AMM market are: Kamino's owner and emergency council can stop redeems, as they did on the ETH reserve for 16 hours; LPs bear Kamino's written-off losses, and bad debt not yet written off is not shown in the rate; swaps larger than the buffer plus Kamino's free liquidity fail.

## Upgrades and freezing

- On devnet the program stays upgradeable under the project's upgrade-authority key, `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/upgrade-authority.json`, as `docs/spec/README.md` sets for every program.
- Intended mainnet upgrade policy: frozen (upgrade authority removed) before any mainnet deployment.
  This departs from the shared default of a multisig with a timelock first: keeping an upgrade key to follow changes in Kamino would be an admin key every LP has to trust, and the in-kind exit already covers a Kamino change.
- A Kamino change that breaks the layout check stops trading in our markets but never traps LPs, who leave in kind; a new strategy version then serves new markets, and LPs move by removing and adding.
- Carrying the policy out belongs to the mainnet launch effort.

## For the shared engineering bar

What `docs/spec/README.md` asks each product's file to add.

### Compute ceilings

Asserted per instruction in test layer 5; the build ticket measures each one and may lower it, and raising one needs a written reason here.

| Instruction | Ceiling (compute units) | Main cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pipeline_quote` | 40,000 | Reserve checks and fixed-point maths; well under the quoter's 200,000 cap |
| `pipeline_swap`, no redeem | 40,000 | One output transfer, the reserve read; the router's own 30k to 35k is outside it |
| `pipeline_swap`, with a redeem | 80,000 | Kamino's redeem (mainnet median 29,670) |
| `pipeline_resolve_accounts` | 40,000 | Runs the quote to decide on the redeem accounts |
| `pipeline_init_market` | 150,000 | Creating two vaults, the cToken account and the LP mint |
| `pipeline_seed_liquidity` | 200,000 | Creation plus the first deposit |
| `add_liquidity` | 60,000 | Two transfers in, an LP mint |
| `remove_liquidity`, cash | 120,000 | Kamino's redeem, transfers out, an LP burn |
| `remove_liquidity`, in kind | 90,000 | Transfers out, possibly creating the LP's cToken account |
| `rebalance` | 100,000 | Kamino's deposit (mainnet median 43,704) or redeem |
| `lock_lp` | 20,000 | One transfer |

### Invariants for test layer 3

Beyond the shared three (value conserved, every holder can exit, each quote equals its swap), checked after every step of the generated sequences, with Kamino's rate moved up between steps and occasionally down by a write-off:

- What the market has recorded never exceeds what it actually holds: the buffer and the other side against their vaults, the cTokens against the cToken account.
- At a fixed Kamino rate, no swap lowers the product `R x L`, and no instruction lowers the value of an LP share; only a fall in Kamino's rate does.
- A removal in kind succeeds for every LP in every Kamino state, emergency modes, a deprecated reserve and a failed layout check included.
- A swap never deposits into Kamino, never redeems when the buffer covers its output, and never redeems more than its shortfall plus one rounding unit's worth of cTokens.
- `rebalance` only ever moves the buffer's share towards `BUFFER_TARGET_BPS`, and never deposits in withdraw mode or while cToken deposits are blocked.
- The share count `N` changes only by `add_liquidity`, `remove_liquidity`, seeding and SPL burns, and the lock account's balance never falls.

### Accepted `pipeline-check` warnings

None.
Exact-out checks are skipped by design and need no reason.

## Devnet

- Our own Kamino lending market, owned by a key in `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/`, with a WSOL reserve and a reserve for our own test USDC mint (6 decimals, mint authority in the same folder), since Circle's devnet USDC cannot be minted freely.
- Setting it up, from the Kamino facts, section 1, as the first devnet script:
  1. `init_lending_market` with our key as owner.
  2. `init_reserve` for each mint, which takes a 100,000 base-unit seed deposit.
  3. While each reserve holds only the seed, `update_reserve_config` with validation skipped for the Pyth price account, the borrow rate curve and a borrow factor of 100.
  4. `update_reserve_config` for the deposit limit, with full validation, which opens deposits.
- Both reserves name the live devnet Pyth feeds (`7UVimffxr9ow1uXYxsr4LHAcV58mLzhmwaeKvJ1pjLiE` for SOL, `Dpw1EAVrSB1ibxiDQyTAW6Zip3J4Btk2x4SgApQCeFbX` for USDC), even though the cToken path never reads them, so a test borrower can open an obligation and create utilisation.
- The sequence has been seen working on devnet (reserve `24EfeXj3XyLLE6GThh8ik4vcxEPMooAU5XXDL5nJHEr8`, 2026-09-14) but not yet run by us.

## Building it

- Generate the program from Pipeline's Apache-2.0 strategy template with `scripts/new-strategy.sh`, from a scratchpad clone at `5ad130d`, and pin the Pipeline crates to `rev = "5ad130d"`, as for the tax AMM.
- Keep the program keypair in `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/`, never in the repo.
- Put every Kamino call and read in one module (deposit, redeem, reserve checks, total supply, what Kamino can pay now, flags), so a later strategy version can add another lending market without touching the pool's maths.
- Write the Kamino instruction data, account lists and reserve offsets by hand from klend 1.28.0, and never depend on the klend crate: klend is BSL 1.1 with no use grant until 2027-11-17, so we call its deployed program but never compile its code into ours.
- Tests load klend's deployed program bytes with cloned mainnet reserve, lending market and mint accounts, as `docs/spec/README.md` (test layer 6) sets.
  A fixture script dumps the accounts once and commits them with the slot they were read at, since an RPC cannot serve an account's past state; it fetches klend's program bytes into a gitignored folder at each setup and checks them against a hash pinned in the repo, as the router's fixture does, so a Kamino upgrade fails the check and is re-pinned deliberately; klend's bytes are never committed.
- Build and test with the toolchain in `docs/toolchain.md` (`source scripts/toolchain-env.sh`).

### Done means

- LiteSVM tests through the real router and the real klend program cover:
  - pricing both ways at LP fees of 0, 30 and 200 bps, and quotes matching swaps on both sides of the buffer's edge;
  - an in-swap redeem: the shortfall, its rounding (the market receives at least the shortfall), and the excess staying in the buffer;
  - an in-swap redeem at one extra outer level (a smart-wallet stand-in program calling the router), with a hooked token (Pipeline's `test-hook`) on the other side;
  - a swap needing a redeem but built without the redeem accounts, failing cleanly;
  - Kamino states made by editing cloned account data: too little free liquidity, the withdrawal cap used up, reserve and market emergency mode, `block_ctoken_usage`, a deprecated reserve, and a reserve failing each part of the layout check, with quotes, swaps, `rebalance`, adding and removing behaving as in the table above;
  - a falling rate from Kamino's real `socialize_loss`, run on an edited obligation that has debt and no collateral, lowering LP share value pro rata;
  - `rebalance`: inside the band, above it, below it, the dust floor, entering and leaving withdraw mode, and deposits skipped under `block_ctoken_usage`;
  - LP shares: the first deposit and its locked minimum, an inflation attempt by donating to the vaults or the cToken account, adding at the ratio, removing in cash and in kind, locking, and an SPL burn;
  - seeding at the seeder-scoped address, shares to the LP recipient, and the vault authority as recipient locking them;
  - refusal of exact-out, of bypass, of every refused mint extension, and of a lent mint not on the list;
  - donations never credited.
